title_en: Hardline Trump aide Stephen Miller takes over as White House chief of staff

body_en: Miller, known as the architect of Trump’s controversial immigration crackdown, is replacing Susie Wiles in new role
Stephen Miller, the architect of Donald Trump’s mass deportation policy and hardline crackdown on immigration, took up his new role as White House chief of staff on Monday.
Miller, 41, began his new role serving as Trump’s right-hand man after Republicans suffered massive losses nationwide in the midterm elections. He was previously serving as a deputy chief of staff.
Stephen Miller, immigration hardliner, in his own words
On Friday, Trump announced on Truth Social that Miller – his most controversial aide – would replace Susie Wiles, his former chief of staff.

The announcement came as a surprise, because members of the Trump administration had denied reports that Wiles was on her way out. In recent weeks, several top women in the administration have stepped down, including Harmeet Dhillon, a top justice department official, and Katie Zacharia, who spent just five days as press secretary after replacing Karoline Leavitt.
Wiles, 69, was the first woman to serve as a White House chief of staff. Trump appointed her to the top White House role after Wiles co-managed his successful 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump gave her the nickname “Ice Maiden” for her calm but no-nonsense approach to managing his agenda and team. Last month, after reports he might replace Wiles, Trump declared there to be “zero chance” that would happen.
Miller’s promotion, and Wiles’s exit, came just days after voters rebuked the US president’s agenda just two years into his administration in the midterm elections .
Democrats accused Trump of not listening to voters by elevating Miller to a top role – especially because Trump’s harsh anti-immigration crackdowns rocked the nation over the last year.
Trump said himself that his mass deportation policy was “too tough” in an interview with CBS’s 60 Minutes which aired over the weekend.
“I think it was too tough,” Trump said. “I think it might be too tough, yeah. And a lot of people would say that it’s great. But a lot of people think it’s too tough.”
Despite that, Trump chose after the interview to elevate the man behind one of his most controversial policies to a larger role in the White House.

Miller has been one of Trump’s longest and most loyal supporters. During Trump’s first term, he served as an adviser for policies such as separating migrant families at the border and the Muslim travel ban.

In Trump’s second term, Miller has expanded his advisory skillset, becoming an advocate for the administration’s crackdown on anti-Charlie Kirk rhetoric , pressuring colleges and universities to comply with Trump’s anti-DEI mandates and leading strikes against suspected drug-smuggling boats .

Miller is one of the US president’s fiercest advocates, often appearing on network television to bolster the administration’s policies. Earlier this year, Miller insisted the US had the right to take Greenland , drawing rebuke from European officials.

He has faced fierce criticism for defending some of the administration’s most aggressive immigration tactics. After Alex Pretti, an American ICU nurse, was killed in Minnesota during an immigration operation, Miller called Pretti a “would-be assassin” .

More administration staffing changes could be coming soon, in the wake of the midterm results and Miller’s appointment. Richard Walters, a White House deputy chief of staff who was one of Wiles’s closest allies, announced he would also be leaving the administration.

Trump said over the weekend that he had offered Dana White, the head of Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), the White House press secretary role. While he later claimed he was “only kidding”, the pair are due to meet on Monday.
body_zh: 米勒被称为特朗普备受争议的移民镇压行动的策划者，他将接替苏西·威尔斯担任新角色
唐纳德·特朗普大规模驱逐政策和强硬镇压移民的设计师斯蒂芬·米勒周一就任白宫办公厅主任。
Miller, 41, began his new role serving as Trump’s right-hand man after Republicans suffered massive losses nationwide in the midterm elections.此前，他曾担任副参谋长。
移民强硬派斯蒂芬·米勒（Stephen Miller）用他自己的话说
周五，特朗普在《真相社会》上宣布，他最具争议的助手米勒将接替他的前幕僚长苏西·怀尔斯。
这一消息令人意外，因为特朗普政府成员否认了有关怀尔斯即将离职的报道。最近几周，政府中的几位女性高层辞职，其中包括司法部高级官员哈米特·迪隆(Harmeet Dhillon)，以及接替卡罗琳·莱维特(Karoline Leavitt)后仅担任新闻秘书五天的凯蒂·扎卡里亚(Katie Zacharia)。
69 岁的怀尔斯是第一位担任白宫办公厅主任的女性。在怀尔斯共同主持成功的 2024 年总统竞选活动后，特朗普任命她担任白宫最高职务。
特朗普给她起了“冰女”的绰号，因为她冷静但严肃地管理他的议程和团队。上个月，在有报道称他可能取代怀尔斯后，特朗普宣布这种情况发生的“可能性为零”。
就在米勒升职和怀尔斯退出的几天前，美国总统在中期选举中就任两年后，选民们对他的议程提出了谴责。
民主党人指责特朗普将米勒提升为最高职位，没有听取选民的意见 — — 特别是因为特朗普去年严厉的反移民镇压震惊了全国。
特朗普在接受哥伦比亚广播公司周末播出的《60 分钟》节目采访时表示，他的大规模驱逐政策“过于严厉”。
“我认为这太艰难了，”特朗普说。 “我认为这可能太难了，是的。很多人会说这很棒。但很多人认为这太难了。”
尽管如此，特朗普在接受采访后还是选择将这位最有争议的政策背后的人提拔到白宫担任更重要的角色。
米勒是特朗普最长期、最忠实的支持者之一。在特朗普的第一个任期内，他担任边境分离移民家庭和穆斯林旅行禁令等政策的顾问。
在特朗普的第二个任期内，米勒扩大了他的咨询技能，成为政府打击反查理·柯克言论的倡导者，向学院和大学施压，要求其遵守特朗普的反 DEI 指令，并领导对涉嫌毒品走私船只的打击。
米勒是美国总统最激烈的支持者之一，经常出现在网络电视上以支持政府的政策。今年早些时候，米勒坚称美国有权占领格陵兰岛，此举遭到欧洲官员的谴责。
他因捍卫政府一些最激进的移民策略而面临激烈批评。美国重症监护室护士亚历克斯·普雷蒂在明尼苏达州的一次移民行动中被杀后，米勒称普雷蒂是“潜在的刺客”。
在中期结果公布和米勒的任命之后，更多的行政人员配置可能很快就会出现。怀尔斯最亲密的盟友之一、白宫副幕僚长理查德·沃尔特斯宣布他也将离开政府。
特朗普周末表示，他已邀请终极格斗锦标赛（UFC）负责人达纳·怀特（Dana White）担任白宫新闻秘书一职。虽然他后来声称自己“只是在开玩笑”，但两人定于周一见面。

title_en: Trump says his deportation policy 'might have been too tough' for voters in the election
title_zh: 特朗普表示，他的驱逐政策对于选举中的选民来说“可能过于严厉”
summary: President Donald Trump said he thinks his administration was too aggressive on deportations
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他认为他的政府在驱逐出境问题上过于激进
body_en: President Donald Trump said he thinks his administration was too aggressive on deportations
By MIKE CATALINI Associated Press and DARLENE SUPERVILLE Associated Press

President Donald Trump , in his first major interview since his party lost control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, said he thinks his administration was too aggressive on deportations and that he thinks he can work with Democrats in the new Congress on some kind of immigration deal.
Trump said his deportation policy was part of the reason Republicans lost, telling CBS’s “60 Minutes” in an interview that aired on Sunday: “I think it might be too tough, yeah.”

He added that he thinks he could reach an agreement with the new Democratic majority. “The deal would be we would work something out. And I think it’s something -- I think that’s something that’s actually doable,” he said in the interview.

Trump did not give specifics about what that deal would look like — and shortly after taping the interview on Friday, Trump named the key architect of his hard-line immigration agenda, Stephen Miller, as his new chief of staff.

“Trump says his immigration crackdown went too far,” Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer scoffed on social media Sunday after the interview aired. “Apparently, his solution was to put the man responsible for it in charge of the White House. That’s not a course correction. That’s a promotion.”

The president's immigration crackdown was a prominent feature of his return to office with major operations in multiple cities sending arrests soaring . Two U.S. citizens — Renee Good and Alex Pretti — were killed by federal officers during protests against the operations.
Democrats have said oversight of Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Department of Homeland Security is a priority for the new Congress.

Trump said he believes that “killers” and “drug dealers” in the country illegally should be deported, but suggested he was open to the idea of a deal that would let others stay “if they’re good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes.”
On the race among Republicans to succeed him for the 2028 presidential election, Trump hinted at staying neutral.
Asked whether he’d endorse a potential successor, the president said “probably, not necessarily.”
“We have a tremendous bench. I have so many people that I have great relationships with,” Trump said in the interview.

Asked about possible candidates other than Vice President JD Vance, Trump only named Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is viewed as a possible 2028 contender.
“I think Marco’s great,” Trump said. “But there are many others and I’d rather not mention their names. There’s some senators that are excellent. I know ’em all, I like ’em a lot.
“So I may or may not get involved. I don’t know. Maybe I’m better off not getting involved,” Trump said.

During the midterms, Democrats sought to make the president’s personal wealth a campaign issue. About half of voters nationally said government corruption was “crucial” for their vote for Congress, according to the AP Voter Poll .
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他认为他的政府在驱逐出境问题上过于激进
迈克·卡塔利尼 (MIKE CATALINI) 美联社和达琳·苏珀维尔 (DARLENE SUPERVILLE) 美联社报道
唐纳德·特朗普总统在他的政党在中期选举中失去参众两院控制权以来的首次重要采访中表示，他认为他的政府在驱逐出境问题上过于激进，他认为他可以与新国会中的民主党人就某种移民协议进行合作。
特朗普表示，他的驱逐政策是共和党失败的部分原因，他在周日播出的哥伦比亚广播公司“60分钟”节目中接受采访时表示：“我认为这可能太艰难了，是的。”
他补充说，他认为他可以与新的民主党多数派达成协议。 “协议是我们会解决一些问题。我认为这是实际可行的，”他在采访中说。
特朗普没有详细说明该协议的具体内容，在周五录制采访后不久，特朗普任命其强硬移民议程的关键设计师斯蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)为他的新任幕僚长。
“特朗普说他的移民镇压太过分了，”周日采访播出后，参议院民主党领袖查克·舒默在社交媒体上嘲笑道。 “显然，他的解决方案是让负责此事的人掌管白宫。这不是路线修正。这是晋升。”
总统的移民镇压是他重返办公室的一个显着特点，在多个城市开展的大规模行动导致逮捕人数激增。两名美国公民蕾妮·古德 (Renee Good) 和亚历克斯·普雷蒂 (Alex Pretti) 在针对此次行动的抗议活动中被联邦官员杀害。
民主党人表示，对移民和海关执法局以及国土安全部的监督是新国会的首要任务。
特朗普表示，他认为该国的非法“杀手”和“毒贩”应该被驱逐出境，但他表示，他对一项协议的想法持开放态度，允许其他人留下来，“如果他们是在园林绿化公司工作、在酒店工作或做某事的好人，对吧？在某些情况下，纳税。”
在共和党人争夺 2028 年总统选举的接班人之争时，特朗普暗示将保持中立。
当被问及是否会认可潜在的继任者时，总统说“可能，但不一定”。
“我们有一个巨大的替补席。我和很多人都有很好的关系，”特朗普在采访中说。

当被问及副总统 JD 万斯以外的可能候选人时，特朗普只提到了国务卿马可·卢比奥，他被视为 2028 年可能的竞争者。
“我认为马可很棒，”特朗普说。 “但还有很多其他人，我不想提他们的名字。有一些参议员非常出色。我认识他们，我非常喜欢他们。
“所以我可能会或可能不会参与。我不知道。也许我不参与会更好，”特朗普说。
在中期选举期间，民主党人试图将总统的个人财富作为竞选议题。据美联社选民民意调查显示，全国大约一半的选民表示，政府腐败对于他们投票给国会“至关重要”。

title_en: Joe Biden to limit White House memoir promotion due to advancing cancer
title_zh: 乔·拜登因癌症进展而限制白宫回忆录宣传
summary: Former president’s new book Promise Me America provides an inside look at January 6, Covid-19 response and more Joe Biden will undertake only limited promotion of his upcoming White House memoir because of advancing cancer, the former president said in a socia
summary_zh: 前总统的新书《Promise Me America》深入剖析了 1 月 6 日、Covid-19 的应对措施以及更多乔·拜登将仅采取有限行动
body_en: Former president’s new book Promise Me America provides an inside look at January 6, Covid-19 response and more
Joe Biden will undertake only limited promotion of his upcoming White House memoir because of advancing cancer, the former president said in a social media post on Sunday night.

His new book, Promise Me America, which will be published on 17 November, is Biden’s account of a one-term presidency that began in 2021 in the shadow of the insurrection at the US Capitol on 6 January 2021 by supporters of Donald Trump eager to overturn the outgoing Republican president’s defeat by his Democratic rival in the 2020 election.

The deadly invasion of the Capitol as Congress was due to meet to certify Biden’s victory , after a rally near the White House where Trump urged his supporters to go to Congress and “fight” for him, remains a historic shame such that Biden in his book says of the current president that it “should follow him to his grave”.

In the post on X, Biden – who was diagnosed with an “aggressive” form of prostate cancer in May 2025, four months after leaving office – said the number of speaking engagements he can manage in support of his book’s publication will be limited.

“Some days are better than others,” he said. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped.”

Instead, Biden said: “I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves”. He said he and his wife, Jill, were touched and grateful for the support of the American people since his condition became known.

The memoir takes an extensive look at the deadly violence in Washington DC fomented by supporters of Trump, who was seeking to remain in office after his defeat by Biden in the 2020 presidential election.
“Donald Trump led an insurrection,” Biden wrote.
“The rioters weren’t ‘peaceful protesters’. They came armed to stop the official certification of a legitimate election.”

Noting that Trump later pardoned more than 1,500 of those convicted of offenses related to the January 6 riot, Biden said: “To this day, Trump and his supporters continue to preen and posture like they’re supporters of law enforcement.

“Here’s my view: You don’t get to turn a blind eye to cops being punched, speared, sprayed, and brutalized and call yourself a friend of law enforcement. What Trump did on January 6 2021 should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave.”

Trump’s actions since he returned to office in January 2025 also come under Biden’s scrutiny, including the chaotic creation of the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge) that put hundreds of thousands of people out of work but failed to yield touted savings.
“All presidents must confront a feeling that their legacy is vulnerable to the pendulum of politics and the whims of their successors,” Biden wrote.

“In my case, that feeling was magnified by the dismissive and destructive nature of Donald Trump, who seemed unable to tolerate the idea that someone else’s accomplishments might be worth building on rather than tearing down.”

Biden, in the post, said the book explores “the challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them”, covering a pivotal period in US history including the Covid pandemic, economic troubles and trying to restore alliances and relationships with allies frayed during Trump’s first term.
Biden said he realized as soon as Trump took office again, much of what he had worked to achieve was soon to be dismantled.
“Trump, he said, “took a wrecking ball to our traditions.” Biden previously published a memoir called Promise Me, Dad, about the death of his elder son, Beau, from cancer.
body_zh: 前总统的新书《Promise Me America》深入剖析 1 月 6 日、Covid-19 应对措施等
这位前总统周日晚上在社交媒体上发帖表示，由于癌症病情恶化，乔·拜登将仅对他即将出版的白宫回忆录进行有限的宣传。
他的新书《Promise Me America》将于 11 月 17 日出版，书中讲述了拜登从 2021 年开始的一届总统任期，当时唐纳德·特朗普的支持者在 2021 年 1 月 6 日美国国会大厦发生了起义，他们渴望推翻这位即将卸任的共和党总统在 2020 年大选中被民主党对手击败的局面。
特朗普在白宫附近举行集会，敦促他的支持者前往国会并为他“战斗”，国会即将召开会议以证明拜登的胜利，国会大厦遭到致命入侵，这仍然是一个历史性的耻辱，以至于拜登在他的书中谈到现任总统时说，它“应该跟随他直到他的坟墓”。
拜登于 2025 年 5 月，即卸任四个月后被诊断出患有“侵袭性”前列腺癌，在 X 上的帖子中表示，他为支持新书出版而能够进行的演讲次数将受到限制。
“有些日子比其他日子好，”他说。 “它并没有阻止我。但有时它会让我放慢脚步。不幸的是，这意味着我将无法像我希望的那样就我的书进行多次对话。”
相反，拜登说：“我希望页面上的文字能够说明一切”。他说，自从他的病情被曝光以来，他和他的妻子吉尔对美国人民的支持感到感动和感激。
该回忆录广泛审视了特朗普的支持者在华盛顿特区煽动的致命暴力事件，特朗普在 2020 年总统选举中输给拜登后寻求继续留任。
“唐纳德·特朗普领导了一场叛乱，”拜登写道。
“骚乱者不是‘和平抗议者’。他们武装起来是为了阻止官方对合法选举的认证。”
拜登指出，特朗普后来赦免了 1500 多名因 1 月 6 日骚乱相关罪行而被定罪的人，他说：“直到今天，特朗普和他的支持者继续打扮得像执法部门的支持者一样。
“我的观点是：你不能对警察遭到拳打、矛刺、喷洒和残暴对待视而不见，还称自己是执法部门的朋友。特朗普在 2021 年 1 月 6 日所做的事情永远不应该被忘记。这应该跟随他直到他的坟墓。”
特朗普自2025年1月重返办公室以来的行动也受到拜登的密切关注，包括混乱地设立所谓的“政府效率部”（Doge），该部门导致数十万人失业，但未能带来所谓的节省。
拜登写道：“所有总统都必须面对这样一种感觉，即他们的政治遗产很容易受到政治摆荡和继任者一时兴起的影响。”
“就我而言，唐纳德·特朗普的轻蔑和破坏性本性放大了这种感觉，他似乎无法容忍别人的成就可能值得巩固而不是摧毁的想法。”
拜登在帖子中表示，这本书探讨了“我们面临的挑战、我做出的决定以及我为什么做出这些决定”，涵盖了美国历史上的一个关键时期，包括新冠疫情、经济困难以及试图恢复与特朗普第一任期内受损的盟友的联盟和关系。
拜登表示，一旦特朗普再次上任，他就意识到，他努力实现的大部分目标很快就会被拆除。
他说，“特朗普对我们的传统造成了破坏。”拜登此前出版了一本名为《爸爸，答应我》的回忆录，讲述了他的大儿子博因癌症去世的故事。

title_en: Joe Biden, in White House memoir, says Trump should carry the weight of Jan. 6 riots 'to his grave'
title_zh: 乔·拜登在白宫回忆录中表示，特朗普应该将 1 月 6 日骚乱的重担“带进坟墓”
summary: Former U_S_ President Joe Biden writes in his White House memoir that Donald Trump has deeply damaged the country and world with an administration determined to “tear down institutions and inflame hatreds.”
summary_zh: 美国前总统乔·拜登在白宫回忆录中写道，唐纳德·特朗普的政府行为严重损害了国家和世界。
body_en: Former U_S_ President Joe Biden writes in his White House memoir that Donald Trump has deeply damaged the country and world with an administration determined to “tear down institutions and inflame hatreds.”

ATLANTA -- Former U.S. President Joe Biden writes in his White House memoir that Donald Trump, at once his predecessor and successor, has deeply damaged the country and world with an administration determined to “tear down institutions and inflame hatreds.”
And the 83-year-old Democrat said the 80-year-old Trump's years of lies about his 2020 defeat to Biden and the Jan. 6 attacks on the Capitol should “follow him to his grave.”

Biden's sweeping indictment comes in the first excerpt of “Promise Me, America,” published Monday by The Atlantic. The 46th president's full memoir is set for a Nov. 17 release. Biden said that while doctors are encouraged by his response to cancer treatment , his activities promoting the book will be limited because of his health.

“Donald Trump led an insurrection," Biden wrote of the attack by Trump supporters as the U.S. Congress met to certify the 2020 election won by the Democrat. "His goal was to remain in power after the American people had voted him out of office.

“The rioters weren’t ‘peaceful protesters," he wrote. “They came armed to stop the official certification of a legitimate election.” He chided Trump for later issuing more than 1,500 pardons of the offenders.

“To this day, Trump and his supporters continue to preen and posture like they’re supporters of law enforcement,” Biden wrote. “Here’s my view: You don’t get to turn a blind eye to cops being punched, speared, sprayed, and brutalized and call yourself a friend of law enforcement. What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave.”
Biden also laments Trump's Department of Government Efficiency and his aggressive reversal of many of his policies, especially those intended to address climate change.

“All presidents must confront a feeling that their legacy is vulnerable to the pendulum of politics and the whims of their successors,” Biden wrote. “In my case, that feeling was magnified by the dismissive and destructive nature of Donald Trump, who seemed unable to tolerate the idea that someone else’s accomplishments might be worth building on rather than tearing down.”

The memoir's release comes on the heels of Biden's fellow Democrats trouncing Republicans in the midterm elections, securing stunningly broad House and Senate majorities and flipping control of several statehouses in a comprehensive rebuke of Trump's second presidency. But Trump's return to power two years earlier was itself a rejection of Biden's one White House term, and many voters still harbor skeptical views of his presidency and his party.
In a lengthy social media post on Sunday, Biden pitched his memoir as the best way he can explain his presidency, “the challenges we faced, the decisions I made and why I made them.”

During his four years in office, Biden confronted the COVID-19 pandemic and its economic fallout, and he worked to restore global alliances that Trump frayed. But he faced widespread concerns about his age, and he abandoned his reelection bid after a disastrous June 2024 debate with Trump. Dogged by lingering inflation and other concerns, Biden’s vice president, Kamala Harris, lost to Trump that November.

Months after leaving office, Biden announced that he'd been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He opened up about his condition in his Sunday social media post, saying he “won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped” and urging people to let the book speak for him.
Biden said his doctors “continue to be encouraged by how I've responded to treatment.” But, he acknowledged, “Some days are better than others. It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down.”

“‘You know, Joe, if it weren't for politics, I believe we'd be good friends,’” Trump said, according to Biden.
body_zh: 美国前总统乔·拜登在他的白宫回忆录中写道，唐纳德·特朗普的政府决心“摧毁机构并煽动仇恨”，从而严重损害了国家和世界。
亚特兰大——美国前总统乔·拜登在他的白宫回忆录中写道，他的前任和继任者唐纳德·特朗普的政府决心“摧毁机构并煽动仇恨”，这对国家和世界造成了严重损害。
这位 83 岁的民主党人表示，80 岁的特朗普多年来关于 2020 年输给拜登以及 1 月 6 日国会大厦袭击事件的谎言应该“跟随他进入坟墓”。
拜登的全面起诉书来自《大西洋月刊》周一发表的《美国，请答应我》的第一篇摘录。第 46 任总统的完整回忆录将于 11 月 17 日出版。拜登表示，虽然医生对他对癌症治疗的反应感到鼓舞，但由于他的健康状况，他宣传这本书的活动将受到限制。
在美国国会开会确认民主党赢得 2020 年大选时，拜登在谈到特朗普支持者的攻击时写道，“唐纳德·特朗普领导了一场叛乱”。 “他的目标是在美国人民投票让他下台后继续掌权。
“骚乱者不是‘和平抗议者’，”他写道。 “他们武装起来阻止合法选举的官方认证。”他指责特朗普后来赦免了 1,500 多名罪犯。
拜登写道：“直到今天，特朗普和他的支持者继续打扮得漂漂亮亮，摆出一副执法支持者的样子。” “我的观点是：你不能对警察遭到拳打、矛刺、喷洒和虐待视而不见，还称自己是执法部门的朋友。特朗普在 2021 年 1 月 6 日所做的一切不应该被忘记。这应该跟随他直到他的坟墓。”
拜登还对特朗普的政府效率部以及他对其许多政策的激进逆转表示遗憾，特别是那些旨在应对气候变化的政策。
拜登写道：“所有总统都必须面对这样一种感觉，即他们的政治遗产很容易受到政治摆荡和继任者一时兴起的影响。” “就我而言，唐纳德·特朗普的轻蔑和破坏性本性放大了这种感觉，他似乎无法容忍别人的成就可能值得巩固而不是摧毁的想法。”
在这本回忆录发布之前，拜登的民主党同僚在中期选举中击败了共和党，获得了众议院和参议院惊人的广泛多数席位，并在对特朗普第二任总统的全面谴责中翻转了对几个州议会的控制权。但特朗普两年前重新掌权本身就是对拜登一个白宫任期的拒绝，许多选民仍然对他的总统任期和他的政党心存怀疑。
在周日的一篇长篇社交媒体帖子中，拜登将他的回忆录视为他解释自己总统任期的最佳方式，“我们面临的挑战、我做出的决定以及我为什么做出这些决定。”
在任职四年期间，拜登应对了新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 大流行及其经济影响，并努力恢复被特朗普破坏的全球联盟。但他面临着对其年龄的广泛担忧，并在 2024 年 6 月与特朗普进行了一场灾难性的辩论后放弃了连任竞选。受挥之不去的通货膨胀和其他担忧的困扰，拜登的副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris) 同年 11 月输给了特朗普。
卸任几个月后，拜登宣布他被诊断出患有前列腺癌。他在周日的社交媒体帖子中公开了自己的病情，称他“将无法像我希望的那样就我的书进行多次对话”，并敦促人们让这本书为他说话。
拜登说，他的医生“继续对我对治疗的反应感到鼓舞”。但是，他承认，“有些日子比其他日子更好。这并没有阻止我。但有时它会让我放慢脚步。”

body_en: Up First briefing: Stephen Miller; Trump; Congress; Nvidia; COP31 : NPR

Up First briefing: Stephen Miller; Trump; Congress; Nvidia; COP31 Republicans have just weeks left of control of Congress. Here's what to expect. And, Trump has appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling his readiness to confront his opposition.
Your support helps make our show possible and unlocks access to our sponsor-free feed.
Trump's Post-Midterm Changes, Lame-Duck Congress, Nvidia Huang Investigation

President Trump has appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff , replacing Susie Wiles. It's Trump's first major personnel change since the Republicans' defeat in the midterms. Miller, who was deputy chief of staff, has been key in shaping many of Trump's controversial policies, particularly on immigration. Voter data indicates that the Democrats gained support partly due to Trump's immigration enforcement.

White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles (R) waves while walking to board Air Force One with White House communications aide Danielle Alvarez (L) and White House Deputy Chief of Staff and Homeland Security Advisor Stephen Miller on October 23, 2026 at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland. Alex Wong/Getty Images hide caption

🎧 Miller supports unchecked executive power. By selecting him, Trump is signaling his readiness to confront an opposition Congress, NPR's Mara Liasson tells Up First . The president has also posted on social media that he offered the White House Press Secretary job to Dana White, the CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship. He later said it was a joke. As president, the public takes his words seriously, and the fact that people cannot take his statements at face value poses a challenge for the U.S., Liasson says.

The 119th Congress is reaching its final weeks before a new Democrat-controlled House and Senate step in. Lawmakers' key agenda item is keeping the federal government open , as funding runs out on Dec. 11. They will likely use a short-term continuing resolution to extend funding, because they lack the time and political will to negotiate the typical 12 appropriations bills.

🎧 Attendance could be a problem for many of the Republicans defeated in the midterms, NPR's Eric McDaniel says. With only a two-vote majority in the House, any absenteeism could jeopardize Republican plans to end their time in power on their own terms. McDaniel says Senate Republicans will likely want to confirm as many judges and Trump appointees as possible before Democrats take over in January. Once the Democrats take control, McDaniel says those confirmations won't happen without significant compromises from the White House.

Massive artificial intelligence chip maker Nvidia is launching an internal investigation after reports that its CEO was involved in a close relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. The New York Times reported that a Chinese intelligence operation targeted Jensen Huang to send advanced Nvidia AI chips to China . NPR reached out to the Chinese Embassy in Washington, D.C., for comment but has not received a response. China denied the allegations on Monday in a press briefing.

🎧 Nvidia plays a crucial role in the U.S. economy as a leading company at the center of the AI revolution, NPR's John Ruwitch says. Huang has significant access to Trump, communicating frequently and even traveling to China with him. When asked about Huang and the incident, Trump said he thinks "Huang is a fine person." The U.S. restricts exports of advanced chips to China, including Nvidia's best chips. Huang has argued that allowing China to buy these chips would slow the growth of its chipmaking industry and benefit America. Despite ongoing investigations, Nvidia believes that neither national security nor its secrets are compromised. The House of Representatives has requested a closed-door briefing from Huang regarding his interactions with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

Climate change is transforming the vibrant colors of nature, from Arctic landscapes to coral reefs. The effects of these color shifts are complex, and scientists are racing to understand them. Here's how climate change is altering the colors of the world

➡️ Every summer, climate-driven wildfires blanket Arctic ice in soot. These dark particles from oil and gas operations, commercial shipping and tourism absorb heat from the sun, accelerating melting ice and contributing to sea-level rise.

➡️ As permafrost thaws deeper into the soil, nutrients become more available, enabling larger vegetation to take hold and turning the landscape greener. A 2020 study in Nature Communications found that about 38% of sites in Alaska, Canada and western Eurasia showed greening.

➡️ Thawing permafrost can also mix soil with lake water, turning them darker. A 2021 study in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (PNAS) found green wavelengths in lakes in the boreal Arctic zone declined by 15% from 1984 to 2019, making these lakes appear darker to the naked eye. The darker a lake gets, the more heat it can store.

➡️ Some insects have changed color due to warmer climates. North American male dragonflies are losing wing color, according to a study in PNAS . This helps them stay cooler but also reduces the coloration that attracts females.

A field of colorful wildflowers blankets the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, transforming the world's driest non-polar desert into a vibrant landscape during the rare flowering desert phenomenon, known locally as the Desierto Florido. This extraordinary event occurs when unusually heavy rainfall awakens seeds that have remained dormant beneath the desert soil for years, sometimes decades. Within weeks, thousands of flowers emerge, covering vast stretches of the desert in shades of pink, purple, yellow, and white. The blooms last only a few weeks before the flowers dry out and release their seeds, which remain in the soil until the next rainfall brings the desert back to life. Huasco, Chile, on Wednesday October 21, 2026. Tamara Merino for NPR. Tamera Merino for NPR hide caption

The Atacama Desert in Chile has transformed into a vibrant patchwork of pinks, yellows, lilacs and purples, thanks to the El Niño super cycle. This floral bloom has been the largest and most colorful in at least 30 years. The phenomenon followed unprecedented rainfall that caused flash floods, damaging homes and forcing evacuations. The rain reached deep into the parched ground, awakening millions of dormant seeds, bulbs and tubers. Now, more than 200 species have burst into color, creating a breathtaking spectacle where every crevice is streaked with hues.

特朗普的中期变革、跛脚鸭国会、英伟达黄调查
特朗普总统任命斯蒂芬·米勒为新任幕僚长，接替苏西·怀尔斯。这是自共和党中期选举失败以来特朗普首次进行重大人事变动。曾任副幕僚长的米勒在制定特朗普许多有争议的政策（特别是移民政策）方面发挥了关键作用。选民数据显示，民主党获得支持的部分原因是特朗普的移民执法。
2026 年 10 月 23 日，在马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地，白宫办公厅主任苏西·怀尔斯（右）与白宫通讯助理丹妮尔·阿尔瓦雷斯（左）和白宫副参谋长兼国土安全顾问斯蒂芬·米勒一起步行登上空军一号时挥手致意。亚历克斯·黄/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
🎧 米勒支持不受限制的行政权力。 NPR 的玛拉·利亚森 (Mara Liasson) 告诉《Up First》，通过选择他，特朗普表明他准备好对抗反对派国会。总统还在社交媒体上发帖称，他向终极格斗锦标赛首席执行官达纳·怀特提供了白宫新闻秘书的职位。他后来说这是一个玩笑。利亚森说，作为总统，公众认真对待他的言论，而人们不能相信他的言论的表面意义，这对美国构成了挑战。
第 119 届国会即将进入最后几周，民主党控制的众议院和参议院将介入。议员们的关键议程是保持联邦政府开放，因为资金将于 12 月 11 日耗尽。他们可能会使用短期持续决议来延长资金，因为他们缺乏时间和政治意愿来谈判典型的 12 项拨款法案。
NPR 的埃里克·麦克丹尼尔 (Eric McDaniel) 表示，对于许多在中期选举中失败的共和党人来说，出席率可能是一个问题。由于众议院只有两票多数，任何缺席都可能危及共和党按照自己的方式结束执政时间的计划。麦克丹尼尔表示，参议院共和党人可能希望在民主党一月份上任之前确认尽可能多的法官和特朗普任命的人选。麦克丹尼尔表示，一旦民主党取得控制权，如果白宫没有做出重大妥协，这些确认就不会发生。
大型人工智能芯片制造商英伟达 (Nvidia) 正在启动内部调查，此前有报道称，该公司首席执行官与一名被指控为中国间谍的女性有密切关系。 《纽约时报》报道称，中国情报部门的目标是黄仁勋向中国发送先进的 Nvidia 人工智能芯片。美国国家公共广播电台联系了中国驻华盛顿大使馆请其置评，但尚未收到回复。中国在周一的新闻发布会上否认了这些指控。

NPR 的约翰·鲁维奇 (John Ruwitch) 表示，作为人工智能革命中心的领先公司，英伟达在美国经济中发挥着至关重要的作用。黄与特朗普有很多接触，经常沟通，甚至与他一起前往中国。当被问及黄和这起事件时，特朗普表示，他认为“黄是一个好人”。美国限制向中国出口先进芯片，包括英伟达最好的芯片。黄仁勋认为，允许中国购买这些芯片将减缓其芯片制造业的增长，并使美国受益。尽管调查仍在进行中，英伟达认为国家安全及其机密都没有受到损害。众议院已要求黄先生就他与一名可疑的中国情报人员的互动情况进行闭门简报。
气候变化正在改变大自然的鲜艳色彩，从北极景观到珊瑚礁。这些颜色变化的影响很复杂，科学家们正在竞相了解它们。气候变化如何改变世界的颜色
➡️ 每年夏天，气候驱动的野火都会用烟灰覆盖北极冰层。这些来自石油和天然气作业、商业航运和旅游业的黑色颗粒吸收太阳的热量，加速冰层融化，导致海平面上升。
➡️ 随着永久冻土融化到土壤深处，养分变得更加可用，使更大的植被得以生长，并使景观变得更加绿化。 《自然通讯》2020 年的一项研究发现，阿拉斯加、加拿大和欧亚大陆西部约 38% 的地点出现了绿化。
➡️永久冻土融化也会使土壤与湖水混合，使它们颜色变深。 《美国国家科学院院刊》(PNAS) 2021 年的一项研究发现，从 1984 年到 2019 年，北极北部地区湖泊的绿色波长下降了 15%，使得这些湖泊肉眼看起来更暗。湖泊颜色越深，储存的热量就越多。
➡️一些昆虫由于气候变暖而变色。根据美国国家科学院院刊的一项研究，北美雄性蜻蜓的翅膀颜色正在消失。这有助于它们保持凉爽，但也减少了吸引雌性的体色。

智利北部的阿塔卡马沙漠上覆盖着一片色彩缤纷的野花，在罕见的开花沙漠现象（当地称为“沙漠沙漠”）期间，将世界上最干燥的非极地沙漠变成了充满活力的景观。当异常的强降雨唤醒了沙漠土壤下休眠多年甚至数十年的种子时，就会发生这种非同寻常的事件。几周之内，成千上万的花朵绽放出来，将大片沙漠覆盖成粉红色、紫色、黄色和白色的色调。花朵只持续几周，然后花朵就会干燥并释放出种子，种子会留在土壤中，直到下一次降雨使沙漠恢复生机。智利瓦斯科，2026 年 10 月 21 日星期三。NPR 的塔玛拉·梅里诺 (Tamara Merino)。 NPR 的 Tamera Merino 隐藏标题栏

body_en: Trump says US war in Iran ‘effectively over’ as he plays down escalation concerns | Donald Trump
President, after talks with Qatari PM, suggests end to war coming ‘fairly soon’ and military escalation not needed
Donald Trump has said that the war in Iran is “effectively over” as he played down concerns that the US would escalate its military campaign against Tehran after the midterm elections.
During a White House press conference, Trump said that Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.

“At this point, taking the military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing – but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason,” he told reporters during a briefing at the White House.

The remarks followed talks in the Oval Office with the Qatari prime minister, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who has lobbied Trump alongside other Gulf countries not to resume the fighting against Iran.
“We’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon,” he added.
Trump has frequently exaggerated claims about the status of negotiations with Iran, saying a final peace deal was imminent dozens of times during the nearly nine-month long war.

The US had continued to move troops to the Middle East in the run-up to the midterm elections. There was speculation that the Trump administration was waiting for the elections to take place before resuming a military campaign, in order to prevent a backlash at the polls.

Republicans were nevertheless routed in a historic defeat in which they lost both houses of Congress, with the vice-president, JD Vance, declaring soon after that the Iran war was a key reason for the defeats.

Trump earlier on Monday said on Truth Social that the leaders of Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait would prefer the “status quo, in other words, a continuation of the Greatest Naval Blockade in History”.
He repeated a mantra that Iran would not be allowed to develop a nuclear weapon, and added that if the situation changed then the US was ready to resume full-scale military action against Iran.

“At this point, however, that seems to be quite unlikely,” he continued. “Israel, and the entire Middle East, are protected from Iranian danger and threats. We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected. At the conclusion of this Military Engagement, the American People, and the World, will be far safer and more secure.”
body_zh: 特朗普表示，美国在伊朗的战争“实际上已经结束”，他淡化了对局势升级的担忧唐纳德·特朗普
总统在与卡塔尔总理会谈后建议“很快”结束战争，不需要军事升级
唐纳德·特朗普表示，伊朗战争“实际上已经结束”，他淡化了人们对中期选举后美国将升级对德黑兰军事行动的担忧。
特朗普在白宫新闻发布会上表示，以色列和该地区的海湾盟友得到了很好的保护，免受伊朗威胁，不需要升级。
他在白宫举行的新闻发布会上对记者说：“目前看来，采取军事行动并不是一件非常必要的事情，但我们已经上膛，准备好以任何理由出发。”
在此之前，卡塔尔首相穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉赫曼·阿勒萨尼在椭圆形办公室举行了会谈，后者一直游说特朗普和其他海湾国家不要恢复针对伊朗的战斗。
“我们看到这场冲突即将结束的势头。我认为它很快就会结束，”他补充道。
特朗普经常夸大与伊朗谈判的状况，在近九个月的战争中数十次表示最终和平协议即将达成。
在中期选举前夕，美国继续向中东派遣军队。有人猜测，特朗普政府正在等待选举开始，然后再恢复军事行动，以防止民意调查出现强烈反弹。
尽管如此，共和党还是遭遇了一场历史性的失败，他们失去了国会参众两院，副总统万斯不久后就宣称伊朗战争是失败的一个关键原因。
特朗普周一早些时候在《Truth Social》上表示，卡塔尔、沙特阿拉伯、阿联酋、巴林和科威特的领导人更愿意“维持现状，换句话说，延续历史上最大规模的海军封锁”。
他重申了不会允许伊朗发展核武器的口头禅，并补充说，如果情况发生变化，美国准备恢复对伊朗的全面军事行动。
“然而，就目前而言，这似乎不太可能，”他继续说道。 “以色列和整个中东都受到保护，免受伊朗的危险和威胁。我们看到了结束这场冲突的积极势头，并将确保美国的利益始终受到保护。在这次​​军事接触结束时，美国人民和世界将更加安全。”

body_en: Massie files articles of impeachment against Hegseth : NPR
Massie files articles of impeachment against Hegseth The articles accuse Hegseth of "high crimes and misdemeanors," including for waging war against Iran in violation of the War Powers Resolution.

Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY), seen here on September 16, 2026 at the U.S. Capitol, filed articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday. Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images hide caption
Rep. Thomas Massie has reintroduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, setting up a vote in the House of Representatives in the next two days.
The Kentucky Republican's resolution accuses Hegseth of high crimes and misdemeanors and lists eight specific charges against him.
3 charges for illegally waging war against Iran in violation of the War Powers Resolution
1 charge for ignoring laws designed to minimize civilian casualties
1 charge for overseeing "extrajudicial killings" in the Caribbean Sea and Eastern Pacific Ocean with strikes on alleged drug boats
1 charge for suppressing free speech, brought in connection to the effort to punish Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., for a video telling service members they can refuse illegal orders
1 charge for the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro without congressional authorization
1 charge for illegally waging war against Yemen in violation of the War Powers Resolution
Pete Hegseth greets British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting at the Pentagon on Oct. 15, 2026. Hegseth says any effort to impeachment him will fail. Finn Gomez/Getty Images hide caption
Hegseth defended his record at the Pentagon in a video released last Thursday, dismissing Massie's effort as "sham articles of impeachment."
"Didn't work against President Trump and it won't work with me," Hegseth said.
Speaking to reporters during an impromptu press briefing on Monday, Trump expressed support for his embattled Defense Secretary.
"I'll stand by him," Trump said. "He won two wars. He was in charge. We all won."
Massie has long been a staunch critic of Hegseth. During the GOP primary, Hegseth campaigned on behalf of Ed Gallrein, who went on to defeat Massie.
In response to Hegseth calling him a "disgruntled defeated congressman," Massie told reporters on Monday: "Well, he's right about one thing — I'm a defeated congressman. I'm not disgruntled."

title_en: Supreme Court paves way for Trump to build a section of his border wall in the Big Bend area of Texas
title_zh: 最高法院为特朗普在德克萨斯州大本德地区修建一段边境墙铺平道路
summary: The Supreme Court allowed President Donald Trump to move forward with construction of his border wall in the remote Big Bend region of southwest Texas.
summary_zh: 最高法院允许唐纳德·特朗普总统继续在德克萨斯州西南部偏远的大本德地区修建边境墙
body_en: Nov. 9, 2026, 2:54 PM EST / Updated Nov. 9, 2026, 5:55 PM EST
WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday allowed President Donald Trump to move forward with construction of his border wall in the remote Big Bend region of southwest Texas.
Construction there had been challenged by an environmental group and locals who say it would damage the environment and historic sites.
The justices blocked an injunction imposed by a federal judge in Texas that had blocked construction while litigation continues.

In a five-page unsigned decision, the court said that the federal judge who ruled on the issue had no authority to do so, adding that the Trump administration was “extremely likely to prevail” on that point.
The government, the court added, has “compelling interests” when a challenged policy involves border security.
Of the nine justices, only liberal Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented.

The segment of the border adjacent to the Rio Grande is sparsely populated, with the Trump administration saying that 89,000 people have been detained trying to enter the United States there in recent years.

The move was challenged by the Center for Biological Diversity, an environmental organization; Friends of the Ruidosa Church, a nonprofit group dedicated to restoring a historic church in the area; and Danny Miller, a river guide who owns property in the area.

“This horrific decision clears the way for contractors to bulldoze pristine desert and dynamite canyon walls before the courts have even decided whether this destruction is legal,” Laiken Jordahl, one of the environmental group’s lawyers said in a statement.

James Percival, the Department of Homeland Security’s general counsel, welcomed the decision in a post on X , saying the lopsided nature of the vote count shows how wrong the lower court judge had been.
“When we filed in the Supreme Court, I called the district court’s order halting wall construction ‘as unprecedented as it is flawed.’ We just won 8-1,” he said.

The section in question, which the government says would involve 341 miles of construction, includes Big Bend National Park. The legal dispute focuses on three waivers issued by then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem in February and her successor Markwayne Mullin in May and July that allowed the government to evade environmental and conservation laws.
In a court filing, Solicitor General D. John Sauer said Congress in 1996 gave the government “broad authority” to build border infrastructure without getting tied up in red tape.
Lawyers for the challengers said that if construction goes ahead, it would “result in the permanent alteration of an irreplaceable landscape” and “threaten unique historic and cultural resources.”
Contrary to the government’s assertions, the Big Bend area has “the lowest apprehension rates” for migrants anywhere along the border, they added.
Government data shows that Big Bend has the section of the southern border with the lowest number of encounters between federal agents and migrants.
The plaintiffs say that the 1996 law only allows for limited waivers for border construction projects in areas where illegal crossings are pervasive.
U.S. District Judge Kathleen Cardone on Oct. 2 invalidated Noem’s waivers, saying the secretary lacked such sweeping powers.
Cardone declined to put her ruling on hold, prompting the administration to turn to the Supreme Court.
body_zh: 美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 9 日下午 2:54 / 更新于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 9 日下午 5:55
华盛顿——周一，最高法院允许唐纳德·特朗普总统继续在德克萨斯州西南部偏远的大本德地区修建边境墙。
那里的建设受到了环保组织和当地人的质疑，他们表示这会破坏环境和历史遗迹。
法官们阻止了德克萨斯州一名联邦法官颁布的一项禁令，该禁令在诉讼仍在继续的情况下阻止了施工。
在一份长达五页的未签名裁决中，法院表示，对此问题做出裁决的联邦法官无权这样做，并补充说特朗普政府在这一点上“极有可能获胜”。
法院补充说，当一项受到挑战的政策涉及边境安全时，政府有“令人信服的利益”。
在九名法官中，只有自由派法官科坦吉·布朗·杰克逊持反对意见。
毗邻格兰德河的边境地区人烟稀少，特朗普政府表示，近年来有 89,000 人在试图进入美国时被拘留。
此举遭到环保组织生物多样性中心的质疑；鲁伊多萨教堂之友 (Friends of the Ruidosa Church) 是一个非营利组织，致力于修复该地区历史悠久的教堂；丹尼·米勒 (Danny Miller) 是一名河流导游，在该地区拥有房产。
该环保组织的律师之一莱肯·乔达尔在一份声明中表示：“这一可怕的决定为承包商在法庭决定这种破坏是否合法之前推平原始沙漠和炸药峡谷壁扫清了道路。”
国土安全部总法律顾问詹姆斯·珀西瓦尔 (James Percival) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中对这一决定表示欢迎，称计票的不平衡性表明下级法院法官的错误有多大。
“当我们向最高法院提起诉讼时，我称地方法院停止修建围墙的命令‘史无前例，而且存在缺陷’。我们刚刚以 8-1 获胜，”他说。
政府表示，该路段将涉及 341 英里的建设，其中包括大弯国家公园。这场法律纠纷的焦点是时任国土安全部部长克里斯蒂·诺姆 (Kristi Noem) 在 2 月份及其继任者马克韦恩·穆林 (Markwayne Mullin) 在 5 月和 7 月发布的三项豁免，这些豁免允许政府规避环境和保护法。
副检察长约翰·绍尔 (D. John Sauer) 在一份法庭文件中表示，国会于 1996 年授予政府“广泛的权力”来建设边境基础设施，而无需受到繁文缛节的束缚。
挑战者的律师表示，如果建设继续进行，将“导致不可替代的景观永久改变”并“威胁独特的历史和文化资源”。
他们补充说，与政府的说法相反，大本德地区对边境沿线任何地方的移民“逮捕率最低”。
政府数据显示，大本德是南部边境地区联邦特工与移民遭遇次数最少的地区。
原告称，1996年的法律只允许对非法越境普遍存在的地区的边境建设项目给予有限的豁免。
美国地区法官凯瑟琳·卡多内 (Kathleen Cardone) 10 月 2 日宣布诺姆的豁免无效，称国务卿缺乏如此广泛的权力。
卡登拒绝搁置她的裁决，促使政府向最高法院求助。

body_en: Republican Thomas Massie moves to force vote to impeach Pete Hegseth | Pete Hegseth
US representative accuses defense secretary of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers

A Republican lawmaker has moved to force a vote to impeach Pete Hegseth , the US defense secretary, setting the stage for a showdown over one of the most divisive figures inside Donald Trump’s administration.
Thomas Massie, of Kentucky, introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, accusing him of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers.

Massie, an outgoing Republican congressman from Kentucky and vocal critic of the president, argued from the well of the House of Representatives that Hegseth had committed “high crimes and misdemeanors” and “has executed unlawful orders” in office.
Massie is expected to have some Republican support for a vote on articles of impeachment. Under House rules, the vote would have to occur no later than Wednesday.
Massie first introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth on 15 September, but House speaker Mike Johnson called US Congress into recess before it could be heard.

Republicans retain control of the House until new members are seated in January, but House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York – widely expected to ascend to speaker – has said he is a “hard yes” on impeaching Hegseth. “Hegseth has got to go,” Jeffries told ABC News on Sunday.

Hegseth spent the morning on Monday at the Naval War college, announcing an array of changes to military education that he said would enable US military officers “to wage war with such devastating speed, precision and lethality that no adversary dares test American result that’s deterrence – and if they do that, they are completely and utterly destroyed: that we achieve victory”.
But it is the failure to deliver victory that has placed a target on Hegseth’s back.

Trump, vice-president JD Vance and other Republican leaders quickly attributed last week’s historic US midterm election losses by Republicans to the Iran war and its pocketbook effects on otherwise-conservative voters.

Hegseth fired back at his critics in a short video released on Thursday, describing the threat of his impeachment as “all about the politics of personal destruction”, insisting that it “won’t work with me”.

Watchdogs Common Cause and Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington argued that the video is a violation of the Hatch Act, which bars the use of government funds for partisan political purposes.

Massie’s impeachment resolution holds that Hegseth has subverted the power of Congress to declare war with unauthorized attacks on Iran and Yemen; systemically violated laws meant to minimize civilian casualties with the killing of more than 100 children at a school in Iran; and engaged in extrajudicial killings when ordering suspected drug boats in the Caribbean to be sunk and their crews left without rescue.

The resolution also argues that Hegseth’s investigation and threatened prosecution of Senator Mark Kelly, a Democrat, and others for calling for troops to disobey illegal orders was an unconstitutional violation of the first amendment, and alleges that the kidnapping of President Nicolás Maduro of Venezuela was illegal and unconstitutional.
body_zh: 共和党人托马斯·马西 (Thomas Massie) 采取行动强制投票弹劾皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) |皮特·赫格斯
美国代表指责国防部长未经国会授权非法发动战争并滥用职权
一名共和党议员已采取行动，强制投票弹劾美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯(Pete Hegseth)，为唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)政府内部最具分裂性的人物之一的摊牌奠定了基础。
肯塔基州的托马斯·马西提出了针对赫格斯塞斯的八项弹劾条款，指控他未经国会授权非法发动战争并滥用职权。
马西是肯塔基州即将离任的共和党议员，也是总统的直言不讳的批评者，他在众议院表示，赫格塞斯在任期间犯下了“重罪和轻罪”，并且“执行了非法命令”。
预计马西将获得一些共和党人对弹劾条款投票的支持。根据众议院规定，投票必须不迟于周三进行。
Massie 于 9 月 15 日首次提出针对 Hegseth 的弹劾条款，但众议院议长 Mike Johnson 在听取弹劾条款之前就要求美国国会休会。
共和党人将保留对众议院的控制权，直到一月份新议员就任为止，但纽约众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯——普遍预计将成为众议院议长——表示他对弹劾赫格塞斯“强硬同意”。 “赫格斯必须离开，”杰弗里斯周日告诉美国广播公司新闻。
赫格斯周一早上在海战学院宣布了对军事教育的一系列改革，他说这些改革将使美国军官“能够以毁灭性的速度、精确性和杀伤力发动战争，以至于没有对手敢于测试美国的威慑成果——如果他们这样做，他们就会被彻底摧毁：我们取得了胜利”。
但正是未能取得胜利才让赫格塞斯成为了攻击目标。
特朗普、副总统万斯和其他共和党领导人很快将上周共和党在美国中期选举中历史性的失败归咎于伊朗战争及其对保守派选民的钱包影响。
赫格斯在周四发布的一段短视频中回击了批评者，称弹劾他的威胁“完全是为了个人毁灭的政治”，并坚称这“对我不起作用”。
华盛顿的共同事业监督组织和责任与道德公民组织认为，该视频违反了《哈奇法案》，该法案禁止将政府资金用于党派政治目的。
马西的弹劾决议认为，赫格塞斯未经授权袭击伊朗和也门，颠覆了国会宣战的权力；伊朗一所学校100多名儿童被杀，全面违反了旨在尽量减少平民伤亡的法律；并下令击沉加勒比海的疑似贩毒船，并在没有获救的情况下离开船员，进行法外处决。
该决议还认为，赫格塞斯对民主党参议员马克·凯利和其他人呼吁军队违抗非法命令的行为进行调查并威胁起诉，违反了第一修正案，并声称绑架委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗是非法和违宪的。

title_en: John Fetterman to be challenged for Senate seat by democratic socialist born in Gaza
title_zh: 出生于加沙的民主社会主义者将挑战约翰·费特曼竞选参议院席位
summary: Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian American, said he would run in a primary to be the Democratic nominee in 2028 US politics live – latest updates John Fetterman, the maverick Democratic senator who has provoked widespread anger by increasingly siding with Republicans,
summary_zh: 巴勒斯坦裔美国人艾哈迈德·摩尔 (Ahmed Moor) 表示，他将参加 2028 年美国政治直播初选，成为民主党候选人 - 最新动态 John Fetterm
body_en: Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian American, said he would run in a primary to be the Democratic nominee in 2028

John Fetterman, the maverick Democratic senator who has provoked widespread anger by increasingly siding with Republicans, is to be challenged for his Pennsylvania seat by a democratic socialist candidate who is originally from Gaza.
Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian American, said he would run in a primary to be the Democratic nominee in 2028, when Fetterman’s seat is up for re-election.

The move is the first sign of Fetterman’s weakened position in the party since the Democrats won back control of the Senate in last week’s US midterm elections, when the party won at least 54 of the upper chamber’s 100 seats.

The prospect of a comfortable Senate majority in effect eliminates the possibility of Fetterman’s vote being decisive, a relief to Democratic strategists who feared he could no longer be relied on for support on contentious issues.
Fetterman had already caused widespread disillusionment among many Pennsylvania Democrats, who campaigned for him in the 2022 midterms when he ran as a progressive outsider.
But he has sparked anger by, on occasion, speaking out in support of Donald Trump, who in turn has praised Fetterman as “a great guy” and said he would “love” him to become a Republican.

Moor, 42, a writer and journalist who was born in the southern Gaza city of Rafah and has previously written for the Guardian, told the Philadelphia Inquirer that he was “not really running against Fetterman”.
“I’m running for good government. I’m running for the rule of law. I’m running because I believe in America,” he said.

But his Palestinian background throws down the gauntlet to Fetterman’s vocally pro-Israel stance, which has become increasingly strident since the 7 October 2023 attack by Hamas that left about 1,200 people on the Israeli side dead. More than 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza – most women and children – have been killed in Israel’s retaliatory military response.
Fetterman has said he has no intention of leaving the Democrats but strongly suggested would change his mind if the party became “anti-Israel”.

“That’s my red line,” Fetterman said last July. “If the Democratic party becomes official anti-Israel, then that’s when I would force me out. If they make it the official platform of the party, then that’s a much different situation.”
Fetterman has met more often with Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister, than with Philadelphia’s mayor, Cherelle Parker, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer.
Moor, by contrast, said he supports withdrawing US aid from Israel and imposing sanctions aimed at securing equal rights for Palestinians.

Democrats say Moor is unlikely to be the only challenger to Fetterman, who provoked outrage in his own party in September by sending a video message to the Republicans’ midterm convention in Texas in which he praised Pennsylvania’s Republican senator, Dave McCormick.

“I’m pretty confident that you’ll see some bigger, mainstream kind of names, involved,” said Mike Weidinger, a veteran Lancaster county Democrat with state-wide connections, who cited Chris Deluzio, a representative from the Pittsburgh area, and Malcolm Kenyatta, a Pennsylvania state legislator, as likely challengers.
“Generally, people think [Fetterman] either misrepresented himself when he ran the first time, or he changed completely from what he said he was,” said Weidinger.

“We just had an election here in Pennsylvania where a lot of us busted our ass for [Pennsylvania governor Josh] Shapiro and a lot of other people, and he didn’t spend one penny or do one thing for a single Democrat candidate here last week.”
On the possibility of Fetterman joining the Republicans, he added: “If he wants to switch, he can switch. If it would have been 51 to 49, it would have mattered. But it doesn’t matter now.”
body_zh: 巴勒斯坦裔美国人艾哈迈德·摩尔 (Ahmed Moor) 表示，他将参加 2028 年民主党总统候选人初选
特立独行的民主党参议员约翰·费特曼(John Fetterman)因日益站在共和党一边而引发了广泛的愤怒，他在宾夕法尼亚州的席位将受到来自加沙的民主社会主义候选人的挑战。
巴勒斯坦裔美国人艾哈迈德·摩尔 (Ahmed Moor) 表示，他将参加 2028 年民主党初选，届时费特曼的席位将进行连任。
此举是自民主党在上周美国中期选举中夺回参议院控制权以来费特曼在党内地位受到削弱的第一个迹象，当时该党赢得了上议院 100 个席位中的至少 54 个席位。
参议院轻松获得多数席位的前景实际上消除了费特曼投票具有决定性的可能性，这让民主党战略家松了一口气，他们担心在有争议的问题上不再依赖他的支持。
费特曼已经让许多宾夕法尼亚州民主党人普遍失望，他们在 2022 年中期选举中为他竞选，当时他作为进步的局外人参选。
但他有时会公开支持唐纳德·特朗普，从而引发愤怒，而特朗普则称赞费特曼是“一个伟大的人”，并表示他会“爱”他成为一名共和党人。
42 岁的摩尔是一名作家兼记者，出生于加沙南部城市拉法，此前曾为《卫报》撰稿，他告诉《费城问询报》，他“并不是真正与费特曼竞争”。
“我竞选是为了好的政府。我竞选是为了法治。我竞选是因为我相信美国，”他说。
但他的巴勒斯坦背景给费特曼的亲以色列立场带来了挑战，自 2023 年 10 月 7 日哈马斯袭击导致以色列方面约 1,200 人死亡以来，费特曼的亲以色列立场变得越来越强硬。加沙超过 74,000 名巴勒斯坦人（其中大多数是妇女和儿童）在以色列的报复性军事反应中丧生。
费特曼表示，他无意离开民主党，但强烈建议，如果民主党变得“反以色列”，他就会改变主意。
“这是我的红线，”费特曼去年七月说道。 “如果民主党正式反以色列，那么我就会把我赶出去。如果他们把它作为该党的官方纲领，那么情况就会大不相同。”
据《费城问询报》报道，费特曼与以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的会面次数多于与费城市长切雷尔·帕克的会面次数。
相比之下，摩尔表示，他支持美国撤回对以色列的援助，并实施旨在确保巴勒斯坦人平等权利的制裁。
民主党人表示，摩尔不太可能是费特曼的唯一挑战者，费特曼去年 9 月向德克萨斯州共和党中期代表大会发送了一段视频，在视频中赞扬了宾夕法尼亚州的共和党参议员戴夫·麦考密克，这引起了党内的愤怒。
“我非常有信心，你会看到一些更大的、主流的名字参与进来，”在全州范围内拥有联系的兰开斯特县资深民主党人迈克·韦丁格(Mike Weidinger)说，他引用匹兹堡地区的代表克里斯·德鲁齐奥(Chris Deluzio)和宾夕法尼亚州议员马尔科姆·肯雅塔(Malcolm Kenyatta)作为可能的挑战者。
“一般来说，人们认为（费特曼）要么在第一次竞选时歪曲了自己，要么他完全改变了他所说的样子，”魏丁格说。
“我们刚刚在宾夕法尼亚州举行了一场选举，我们中的很多人为[宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什]夏皮罗和许多其他人竭尽全力，而他上周没有为一位民主党候选人花一分钱或做任何事。”
关于费特曼加入共和党的可能性，他补充道：“如果他想改变，他可以改变。如果是51比49，那就很重要了。但现在不重要了。”

title_en: Senate votes on bill to speed up projects from gas pipelines to clean energy
title_zh: 参议院就加速从天然气管道到清洁能源项目的法案进行投票
summary: Environmentalists torn over procedural vote to boost infrastructure projects but weaken environmental laws It’s a bill that would make it easier to build big infrastructure projects in America – everything from fossil fuel pipelines to transmission lines that
summary_zh: 环保人士对促进基础设施项目但削弱环境法的程序性投票产生了分歧。
body_en: Environmentalists torn over procedural vote to boost infrastructure projects but weaken environmental laws

It’s a bill that would make it easier to build big infrastructure projects in America – everything from fossil fuel pipelines to transmission lines that would add more clean energy to the grid. And it would roll back environmental and social protections to achieve this goal. That is why climate advocates are torn over the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs act (Baaja), which is scheduled for an initial procedural Senate vote on Monday.

Donald Trump urged all senators to vote for the 417-page bill, which is sponsored by two Republicans and two Democrats in the Senate, but after last week’s historic “blue wave” elections , some environmental and tribal advocates called on Democratic leadership to pump the brakes.

Earthjustice, Sierra Club and the ACLU have come out against the bill because it would significantly weaken environmental laws including the National Environmental Policy Act (Nepa) and accelerate the construction of gas pipelines and ICE detention centers.

Indigenous groups held a press conference on Friday calling on senators to vote against Baaja because it would weaken the federal government’s legal obligation to consult tribes on projects that affect them. “This is such an existential threat to Indian country,” said Mark Macarro, president of the National Congress of American Indians.

Protesters rallied outside Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer ’s building on Friday over concerns that the bill could boost datacenters. “It would be highly ironic if, having won an election where datacenter opposition was at the front and center, the first act of Congress was to make it easier to build datacenters,” said Bill McKibben .

Democrats elected in the blue wave will not take their seats until January, so the bill’s proponents still have time to rush it through the Senate, and technically there is time for it to pass in the House before new Congress and go to Trump.

But the election success for the Democrats is dialing up the political friction. House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, expected to be the House speaker in the new Congress, said the bill “falls short in several areas” including failing to protect tribal sovereignty, and he would not “rubber-stamp legislation without more constructive involvement with our caucus”.
How Democrats used the midterms to turn affordability concerns into ‘green populism’

On Monday, the bill’s Democratic sponsors, Senators Martin Heinrich and Sheldon Whitehouse, said they had the votes to pass the bill. Heinrich said they had made last-minute changes to ensure tribal consultation, and they believed the bill would favor renewables over fossil fuels. “If we can create an open, competitive level playing field, clean is cheap, and cheap wins in the marketplace,” Heinrich said.

Whitehouse, who wore a tie with wind turbines on it, argued that passing the bill would set the stage for Democrats to work on clean energy policies next year with majorities in the House and Senate. “People should just cool their jets and have a little faith that this is not the end of the story,” he said.

Proponents of Baaja say it is needed because it takes too long to build large projects in America and the bill shortens timelines. It simplifies federal rules for building interstate transmission lines, it narrows what gets reviewed under the National Historic Preservation Act and limits tribal consultation, it limits the use of the Clean Water Act, shortens timelines for the Endangered Species Act, limits how the executive branch can interfere with federal permitting, and makes big changes to Nepa such as changing what requires Nepa review and who has standing to sue.
The fossil fuel industry is backing Baaja. The American Petroleum Institute (API) hailed the bill as “a historic opportunity” and called on congress to “finish permitting reform this year”.

“It creates a very accelerated fast track for gas pipelines,” said Earthjustice Action’s president, Abbie Dillen. “The gas industry is extraordinarily excited about this because they are interested in expanding existing pipeline capacity to get more liquefied natural gas out for export, and to be feeding power-hungry datacenters with gas.”

The bill could help pave the way for the Constitution gas pipeline that Williams Companies is trying to build through New York. The state denied the project’s water quality permit in 2016, but the company has revived the project under the Trump administration. The proposed pipeline could benefit from the bill’s changes to the Clean Water Act.

Baaja could also enable construction of gas pipelines in the west. Fossil fuel advocacy group Western States and Tribal Nations wants to build gas pipelines to feed domestic datacenters and export LNG from the west coast. During a 3 November election day meeting with Wyoming’s Sweetwater county board of commissioners, the advocacy group’s president, Andrew Browning, said he was talking to lawmakers about the bill: “The permitting bill’s a huge thing … We’re going to need that for everything we’re envisioning and building out.”

Some clean energy advocates want the bill to pass because it would connect renewables to the grid. Wind, solar and battery storage are now cheap to build , but the country lacks the necessary transmission lines to bring clean energy where it’s needed.

Interstate transmission lines can take a decade to get built, and energy projects also face a bottleneck in connecting to the grid. At the end of 2025, 2,060 GW of total generation and storage capacity were waiting in a queue to connect to the grid.

body_zh: 环保人士对推动基础设施项目但削弱环境法的程序性投票产生分歧
该法案将使在美国建设大型基础设施项目变得更加容易——从化石燃料管道到将为电网增加更多清洁能源的输电线路。为了实现这一目标，它将取消环境和社会保护措施。这就是为什么气候倡导者对两党美国负担能力和就业法案（Baaja）存在分歧，该法案定于周一在参议院进行初步程序性投票。
唐纳德·特朗普敦促所有参议员投票支持这项长达 417 页的法案，该法案由参议院两名共和党人和两名民主党人发起，但在上周历史性的“蓝色浪潮”选举之后，一些环境和部落倡导者呼吁民主党领导层踩刹车。
地球正义组织 (Earthjustice)、塞拉俱乐部 (Sierra Club) 和美国公民自由联盟 (ACLU) 联合起来反对该法案，因为该法案将大大削弱包括《国家环境政策法案》(Nepa) 在内的环境法，并加速天然气管道和 ICE 拘留中心的建设。
原住民团体周五举行新闻发布会，呼吁参议员投票反对巴哈，因为这将削弱联邦政府就影响部落的项目与部落协商的法律义务。 “这对印度国家来说是一个生死存亡的威胁，”美国印第安人全国代表大会主席马克·马卡罗说。
周五，抗议者在参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 大楼外集会，担心该法案可能会促进数据中心的发展。 Bill McKibben 表示：“如果在赢得一场数据中心反对派占据主导地位的选举后，国会的第一个行动就是让数据中心的建设变得更容易，那将是非常讽刺的。”
在蓝色浪潮中当选的民主党人要到一月份才能就职，因此该法案的支持者仍有时间在参议院匆忙通过该法案，从技术上讲，该法案还有时间在新国会之前在众议院通过并交给特朗普。
但民主党的选举成功加剧了政治摩擦。预计将成为新一届国会众议院议长的众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯表示，该法案“在几个方面存在缺陷”，包括未能保护部落主权，而且他不会“在没有更多建设性参与我们核心小组的情况下就批准立法”。
民主党如何利用中期选举将负担能力担忧转变为“绿色民粹主义”
周一，该法案的民主党发起人、参议员马丁·海因里希和谢尔登·怀特豪斯表示，他们拥有通过该法案的选票。海因里希表示，他们在最后一刻做出了修改，以确保部落协商，他们相信该法案将有利于可再生能源而不是化石燃料。海因里希说：“如果我们能够创造一个开放的、竞争性的公平竞争环境，清洁就是廉价的，廉价的就能赢得市场。”
怀特豪斯戴着一条印有风力涡轮机的领带，他认为通过该法案将为民主党明年在众议院和参议院占多数席位的情况下制定清洁能源政策奠定基础。 “人们应该冷却他们的飞机，并相信这不是故事的结局，”他说。
Baaja 的支持者表示，这是必要的，因为在美国建设大型项目需要很长时间，而该法案缩短了时间。它简化了建设州际输电线路的联邦规则，缩小了《国家历史保护法》的审查范围，并限制了部落协商，限制了《清洁水法》的使用，缩短了《濒危物种法》的时限，限制了行政部门干预联邦许可的方式，并对 Nepa 做出了重大改变，例如改变了 Nepa 审查的要求和起诉资格。
化石燃料行业正在支持巴哈。美国石油协会（API）称赞该法案是“历史性机遇”，并呼吁国会“今年完成许可改革”。
“它为天然气管道创造了一条非常加速的快车道，”地球正义行动主席艾比·迪伦说。 “天然气行业对此感到非常兴奋，因为他们有兴趣扩大现有管道容量，以出口更多液化天然气，并为耗电的数据中心提供天然气。”
该法案可能有助于为威廉姆斯公司试图在纽约修建的宪法天然气管道铺平道路。 2016年，该州拒绝了该项目的水质许可，但该公司在特朗普政府的领导下恢复了该项目。拟议的管道可能会受益于该法案对《清洁水法》的修改。
巴哈还可以在西部建设天然气管道。化石燃料倡导组织西方国家和部落国家希望建造天然气管道，为国内数据中心供电并从西海岸出口液化天然气。在 11 月 3 日选举日与怀俄明州斯威特沃特县委员会举行的会议上，该倡导组织主席安德鲁·布朗宁 (Andrew Browning) 表示，他正在与立法者讨论该法案：“许可法案是一件大事……我们将需要它来实现我们设想和建设的一切。”
一些清洁能源倡导者希望该法案获得通过，因为它将把可再生能源连接到电网。现在风能、太阳能和电池存储的建设成本低廉，但该国缺乏必要的输电线路来将清洁能源输送到需要的地方。
州际输电线路可能需要十年才能建成，能源项目也面临着并网的瓶颈。到 2025 年底，总发电量和存储容量为 2,060 吉瓦，正在排队等待连接电网。

President Trump is shaking up his closest advisers after Democrats made huge gains in the midterm elections.

Yeah. Stephen Miller takes over the role after serving as deputy. And in a moment, we'll discuss the move with a former colleague of Miller. His elevation is the president's first big personnel move since his party suffered an overwhelming defeat in the midterm elections. Susie Wiles, the previous chief of staff, had been seen as something of a calming influence.
INSKEEP: OK. So what does that change tell us about the second half of Trump's second term? We brought in NPR's Mara Liasson, who I think of as a calming influence. Mara, good morning.
MARA LIASSON, BYLINE: Ha, ha, ha. Hi (laughter).
INSKEEP: Anyway, good to hear from you. What has Stephen Miller's role been up to now?

LIASSON: Miller was the deputy chief of staff. Now he's the chief of staff. He's a hard-liner on a number of issues, primarily mass deportations. He's also behind policies to revoke temporary protected status for immigrants from places like Somalia and Haiti. He believes in unchecked executive power. And I think by choosing Miller, Trump is showing that he is ready for a lot of fights with an opposition Congress.
INSKEEP: Well, yeah. But he also said he was going to look for ways to work with Democrats. Does this signal that nah?

LIASSON: Well, I think it signals that he wants to continue a confrontation. Miller has shown no interest in compromise, tells you that Trump wants to double down on his policies. Miller has called Democrats, quote, "extremists and freaks." He's called the Democratic Party a domestic extremist organization.

INSKEEP: And you already mentioned one thing when you talked about revoking temporary protected status. Miller has worked the bureaucracy very hard over two terms, really, finding more and more ways to block both legal and illegal immigrants from the United States. And he's had shouty performances on TV. That's his image.
LIASSON: That's right. Trump said one of the reasons he chose him is because Miller is, quote, "a fighter and very loyal." And here is Miller talking last year about crime in Memphis, Tennessee.

STEPHEN MILLER: The gangbangers that you deal with, they think that they're ruthless. They have no idea how ruthless we are. They think they're tough. They have no idea how tough we are. They think that they're hardcore. We are so much more hardcore than they are. And we have the entire weight of the United States government behind us.
LIASSON: But just last night, Trump said in a "60 Minutes" interview on CBS that his administration's deportation policy may have gone too far. Here he is.
PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: And there's a large group of people think that they should be allowed to stay, so...
ROSS DOUTHAT: So you think your deportation policy went too far?

LIASSON: So there's what he says and what he does. One of Trump's close allies, Roger Stone, said when Trump turned to Miller, it's because he wanted a, quote, "wartime consigliere." And it tells you how Trump is viewing the next two years - fight, fight, fight.

利亚森：没错。特朗普表示，他选择米勒的原因之一是因为米勒是“一名斗士，而且非常忠诚”。米勒去年谈论了田纳西州孟菲斯的犯罪行为。
史蒂芬·米勒：与你打交道的黑帮分子，他们认为自己是无情的。他们不知道我们有多么无情。他们认为自己很坚强。他们不知道我们有多坚强。他们认为自己是硬核。我们比他们硬核得多。我们有美国政府的全力支持。
利亚森：但就在昨晚，特朗普在哥伦比亚广播公司的“60 分钟”采访中表示，他的政府的驱逐政策可能太过分了。他在这里。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：有一大群人认为他们应该被允许留下来，所以......
ROSS DOUTHAT：那么您认为您的驱逐政策太过分了？
利亚森：所以这就是他所说的和他所做的。特朗普的亲密盟友之一罗杰·斯通(Roger Stone)表示，当特朗普转向米勒时，是因为他想要一位“战时军师”。它告诉你特朗普如何看待未来两年——战斗，战斗，战斗。

title_en: Trump Media cashes in on high-speed access to social media posts
title_zh: 特朗普媒体通过高速访问社交媒体帖子获利
summary: Trump Media and Technology Group reported that revenue surged 205%, which it says was “primarily driven” by selling a high-speed feed of posts on Truth Social.
summary_zh: 特朗普媒体和科技集团报告称，收入猛增 205%，称其“主要得益于”Trut 上帖子高速推送的销售
body_en: Trump Media revenue surges on high-speed Truth Social access
Trump Media and Technology Group on Monday reported that revenue surged 205% in the third quarter, which it says was “primarily driven” by selling a high-speed feed of posts on Truth Social.

The “Truth API,” as the company calls it, allows news organizations, Wall Street trading firms and other services to pay between $60,000 and $100,000 per month for a direct feed of posts on the social network. Critics have slammed the feed as an attempt to profit from President Donald Trump’s posts.
Trump, whose revocable trust is the largest single shareholder of Trump Media, is the most prominent user of Truth Social.

The president’s trust owns more than 41% of Trump Media, according to S&P Capital IQ data. In a June SEC filing, the trust said that Donald Trump Jr. was “the sole trustee and has sole voting and investment power” over its holdings.
Trump Media’s stock, which trades under the symbol “DJT” for the president’s initials, closed at $4.06 on Monday, giving it a market valuation of $1.13 billion. It’s down 69% so far this year.
In July, Trump Media announced the high-speed feed offering , saying that it would allow “real-time access to posts from the highest-ranking Truth Social accounts.”

The company acknowledged that the service could be market-moving and highly valuable to any trading firm. “Markets already move on Truth Social posts,” Kevin McGurn, interim CEO of Trump Media, said at the time. He added that “high frequency and algorithmic trading firms that require a low-latency, machine-readable feed rather than manual tracking” could benefit from paying for the feed.
In August, the company said the service had gone live.

Last month, Reuters reported that Bloomberg and two Wall Street trading firms were some of the customers who had signed up for the service. Bloomberg declined to comment to NBC News in October, while the other two firms named did not return a request for comment at the time.

Top Democratic lawmakers, Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Sen. Adam Schiff of California, said the Truth Social feed amounts to “an outrageous abuse of the President’s office for his personal benefit.” In July, the senators asked the Securities and Exchange Commission to “determine whether the proposed arrangement would violate applicable federal securities laws.”
Trump was asked on Sunday if he was using the presidency to enrich himself.

“I devote almost no time to my net worth,” Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes” in an interview. “I have a lotta money, and far more than I ever thought I’d have. And I guess it’s gone up. I don’t even know.”
Trump said his son “watches over” his money, adding: “I don’t even talk to him about it.”

Trump’s personal finances differ vastly from presidents of recent years. In June, Trump’s most recent annual personal financial disclosure spanned more than 900 pages . By comparison, President Barack Obama’s final disclosure form was eight pages, while President Joe Biden’s was 11. Vice President JD Vance’s form for last year is 17 pages.
Trump’s disclosure shows billions of dollars in earnings tied to cryptocurrencies, media settlements, and vast personal investments in stocks and bonds.
The White House has repeatedly insisted that “neither the President nor his family has ever engaged — or will ever engage — in conflicts of interest.”
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.
body_zh: 特朗普媒体收入因高速真相社交访问而激增
特朗普媒体和科技集团周一报告称，第三季度收入猛增 205%，该集团表示，这“主要得益于”Truth Social 上高速帖子的销售。
该公司称之为“Truth API”，允许新闻机构、华尔街贸易公司和其他服务机构每月支付 60,000 至 100,000 美元的费用，以直接在社交网络上发布帖子。批评者猛烈抨击该消息试图从唐纳德·特朗普总统的帖子中获利。
特朗普的可撤销信托是特朗普媒体最大的单一股东，也是 Truth Social 最著名的用户。
根据 S&P Capital IQ 数据，总统的信托基金拥有 Trump Media 超过 41% 的股份。在 6 月份向美国证券交易委员会 (SEC) 提交的文件中，该信托基金表示，小唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump Jr.) 是其持股的“唯一受托人，拥有唯一投票权和投资权”。
特朗普媒体的股票交易代码为总统姓名首字母“DJT”，周一收盘价为 4.06 美元，市值为 11.3 亿美元。今年迄今已下降 69%。
7 月，特朗普媒体宣布推出高速提要服务，称它将允许“实时访问排名最高的 Truth Social 帐户中的帖子”。
该公司承认，这项服务可能会影响市场，并且对任何贸易公司都非常有价值。特朗普媒体临时首席执行官凯文·麦格恩当时表示：“市场已经开始关注真相社交帖子。”他补充说，“需要低延迟、机器可读的数据源而不是手动跟踪的高频和算法交易公司”可以从支付数据源中受益。
八月份，该公司表示该服务已经上线。
上个月，路透社报道称，彭博社和两家华尔街贸易公司是签约该服务的部分客户。彭博社 10 月份拒绝向 NBC 新闻发表评论，而另外两家被点名的公司当时也没有回复评论请求。
民主党高层议员、马萨诸塞州参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦和加利福尼亚州参议员亚当·希夫表示，Truth Social 的推送相当于“为了个人利益而对总统办公室的粗暴滥用”。七月，参议员们要求证券交易委员会“确定拟议的安排是否违反适用的联邦证券法。”
特朗普周日被问及是否利用总统职位为自己谋取利益。
“我几乎没有花时间在我的净资产上，”特朗普在接受哥伦比亚广播公司“60 分钟”采访时说道。 “我有很多钱，比我想象的要多。而且我猜它已经涨了。我什至不知道。”
特朗普表示，他的儿子“看管”他的钱，并补充道：“我什至不跟他谈论这件事。”
特朗普的个人财务状况与近年来的总统有很大不同。 6 月份，特朗普最新的年度个人财务披露长达 900 多页。相比之下，巴拉克·奥巴马总统的最终披露表格为 8 页，而乔·拜登总统的最终披露表格为 11 页。副总统 JD 万斯去年的表格为 17 页。
特朗普的披露显示，数十亿美元的收入与加密货币、媒体和解以及大量个人股票和债券投资相关。
白宫一再坚称，“总统和他的家人都没有——也永远不会——参与利益冲突。”
史蒂夫·科派克 (Steve Kopack) 是 NBC 新闻的资深记者，报道商业和经济问题。

title_en: WATCH: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese agent
title_zh: 观看：特朗普称联邦调查局正在调查英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与涉嫌中国特工的恋情
summary: President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about the FBI looking into his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent.
summary_zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋不应该担心联邦调查局调查他与一名据称是美国女性的女性的恋情。

Huizhong Wu, Associated Press Huizhong Wu, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-trump-says-fbi-is-looking-into-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huangs-affair-with-alleged-chinese-agent
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about the FBI looking into his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent.
President Donald Trump responded to spy plot allegations involving Nvidia's CEO in a White House briefing Monday. Watch his remarks in the player above.
"I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape," Trump said at a White House briefing.

The sudden emergence of Huang's infidelity has rocked the political class and America's tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence.
Trump suggested the extraordinary step of directly involving himself in a counterintelligence investigation, a sign of his friendly relationship with Huang and the possible geopolitical stakes.
"I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right, how you're doing," Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy."
President Donald Trump spoke about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy in a briefing Monday.
Trump is slated to meet next week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, but he was noncommittal about bringing up the situation with Xi.
"No, I don't think so," Trump said. "I mean, maybe. I'm sure President XI will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he's a very honorable man."
China denied on Monday it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, saying the spying allegations were unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing.
Huang has acknowledged he had been intimate with a business executive, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia's website. He did not name the woman.
Nvidia announced Sunday it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort."
The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing.
"I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security," Huang said in his letter.
In a routine news briefing Monday, a Chinese spokesperson rejected claims it used the woman as a spy.
"The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China," Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday.

华盛顿（美联社）——美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋不应该担心联邦调查局调查他与一名据称是中国政府特工的女性的恋情。
唐纳德·特朗普总统在周一的白宫简报中回应了涉及英伟达首席执行官的间谍阴谋指控。观看他在上面播放器中的言论。
特朗普在白宫新闻发布会上表示：“我知道联邦调查局正在从其他方面调查此事，我认为他会状况良好。”
黄的不忠事件的突然出现震惊了政治阶层和美国科技行业，引发了人们对中国是否能够获得英伟达设计的推动人工智能发展的尖端芯片的新担忧。
特朗普建议采取非同寻常的步骤，直接参与反情报调查，这是他与黄的友好关系以及可能的地缘政治利益的标志。
特朗普说：“我今天确实和他谈过，只是想看看他是否感觉还好，你过得怎么样。” “他说他完全不知道这个人是间谍。”
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在周一的新闻发布会上谈到了英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情。
特朗普定于下周在中国深圳举行的亚太经济合作峰会上与中国领导人习近平会面，但他对向习近平提及这一情况不置可否。
“不，我不这么认为，”特朗普说。 “我的意思是，也许吧。我确信十一主席会问我这件事。我非常了解詹森。我只是认为他是一个非常值得尊敬的人。”
中国周一否认试图诱捕黄，称间谍指控未经证实，是针对北京的抹黑活动。
黄仁勋承认他与一名企业高管关系密切，并在英伟达网站上发布的一封公开信中向妻子和公司道歉。他没有透露这名女子的名字。
英伟达周日宣布，正在对有关黄是“外国情报工作目标”的报道进行独立调查。
《纽约时报》报道称，美国情报部门确定该女子正在为北京收集信息。
黄仁勋在信中表示：“我支持调查并将全力配合。我热爱我们的国家和我们的公司。我致力于保护 NVIDIA 并支持美国的国家安全。”

title_en: Trump admin proposes stricter unemployment work search rules
title_zh: 特朗普政府提议更严格的失业工作搜索规则
summary: Under a proposed federal rule, Americans seeking unemployment aid would have to conduct more job searches each week.
summary_zh: 根据拟议的联邦规则，寻求失业援助的美国人每周必须进行更多的求职活动。
body_en: Trump administration proposes stricter work search rules to qualify for unemployment benefits - CBS News
The Trump administration on Monday proposed stiffer rules for Americans seeking unemployment benefits that, if adopted, would require them to conduct more weekly job searches.

The proposed Department of Labor regulations, set to be published in the Federal Register on Tuesday, would require people applying for or collecting jobless aid to complete at least five unique work searches per week. Currently, many U.S. states require two to three qualifying work searches per week, while only four states require five. Some states require only one work search activity to qualify for unemployment benefits.

The Trump administration said the change is necessary to create consistent eligibility requirements for unemployment benefits nationwide. A national minimum weekly work search standard would "improve program integrity and strengthen labor market attachment," the Labor Department said in its proposal.

"This action is necessary to reduce inconsistencies beyond those created by local labor markets in State-level requirements for individuals to actively seek work," according to the agency. "The intended effect is to hold States accountable for administering [an unemployment compensation] program that provides temporary wage replacement to eligible individuals while they are actively seeking work through a meaningful engagement with the labor market."
The public has 60 days following publication of the proposed rule to offer comment.
Labor advocates criticized the proposed change in work search rules, saying the new threshold would be hard for unemployed people to meet and costly for states to administer.

"Not only is the proposed change devastating to claimants who may not have five search options for every week they are unemployed, but it will likely cost states hundreds of thousands of dollars," Michele Evermore, senior director of economic security and worker transitions at the National Employment Law Project, a worker advocacy group, said in a statement to CBS News. "Nearly all states will have to change their claimant intake forms, and with it, their technology — a costly fix. Many states will have to rewrite their laws to meet this rule."

Evermore also said the proposed rule would disadvantage applicants who already struggle to navigate the unemployment benefits systems. Employers "want candidates enthusiastic about their job opportunities, not ticking boxes for the work search form," she added.

The Labor Department acknowledged that the policy could temporarily raise costs as states and jobless aid applicants adapt to the new work requirement, but said the change is necessary to ensure that the eligibility rules are applied consistently across the U.S.

"These inconsistencies can create confusion for individuals, lead to uneven enforcement when allowable activities are not clearly defined, and increase the likelihood that otherwise eligible individuals may fail to meet requirements simply because expectations are unclear," the Labor Department said. "Additionally, variability in how States notify individuals of work search requirements can result in individuals engaging in activities that may not support reemployment or may not satisfy the State's rules."

Various activities would satisfy the proposed requirement that people seeking jobless aid conduct at least five work searches per week, according to the Labor Department. For example, beyond contacting a prospective employer, registering with or contacting a job placement agency or union would also count as a qualified work search.

Under the proposal, states could also designate other activities as satisfying the requirement. Additionally, states could adapt the weekly job search threshold to account for local labor market conditions through a points-based system that would allow someone applying for jobless aid to accrue multiple points for a single activity.
"Under such a system, States may assign point values to qualifying work search activities and require individuals to accumulate a minimum of five points per benefit week," the Labor Department said.

body_zh: 特朗普政府提出更严格的求职规则以获得失业救济金 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
特朗普政府周一对寻求失业救济的美国人提出了更严格的规定，如果获得通过，将要求他们每周进行更多的求职活动。
拟定于周二在《联邦公报》上公布的劳工部法规将要求申请或领取失业援助的人每周至少完成五次独特的工作搜索。目前，美国许多州每周要求两到三次合格的工作搜索，而只有四个州需要五次。一些州只需要一项求职活动就有资格获得失业救济金。
特朗普政府表示，这一改变对于在全国范围内制定一致的失业救济资格要求是必要的。劳工部在其提案中表示，全国每周最低求职标准将“提高计划的完整性并加强劳动力市场的依附性”。
该机构表示：“这一行动对于减少当地劳动力市场在州一级对个人积极寻找工作的要求方面造成的不一致是必要的。” “预期的效果是让各州负责管理[失业补偿]计划，该计划为符合资格的个人提供临时工资替代，同时他们通过有意义地参与劳动力市场来积极寻找工作。”
拟议规则发布后，公众有 60 天的时间提出评论。
劳工权益倡导者批评了求职规则的拟议变更，称新的门槛对于失业者来说很难达到，而且各州的管理成本也很高。
工人权益组织国家就业法项目经济安全和工人过渡高级主任米歇尔·埃弗莫尔在给哥伦比亚广播公司新闻的一份声明中表示，“拟议的改革不仅对失业申请人来说是毁灭性的，因为他们每周失业可能没有五个搜索选项，而且可能会让各州损失数十万美元。” “几乎所有州都必须改变他们的索赔申请表，随之而来的是他们的技术——这是一个代价高昂的解决方案。许多州将不得不重写他们的法律来满足这一规则。”
埃弗莫尔还表示，拟议的规则将使那些已经难以适应失业救济制度的申请人处于不利地位。她补充说，雇主“希望候选人对他们的工作机会充满热情，而不是在求职表上打勾”。
劳工部承认，随着各州和失业援助申请人适应新的工作要求，该政策可能会暂时增加成本，但表示这一改变是必要的，以确保资格规则在美国各地一致适用。
劳工部表示：“这些不一致可能会给个人带来困惑，在没有明确定义允许的活动时导致执法不均，并增加原本符合资格的个人仅仅因为期望不明确而无法满足要求的可能性。” “此外，各国通知个人求职要求的方式存在差异，可能会导致个人从事可能不支持再就业或不符合国家规定的活动。”
据劳工部称，各种活动将满足拟议的要求，即寻求失业援助的人每周至少进行五次求职。例如，除了联系未来的雇主之外，向就业安置机构或工会注册或联系也算作合格的求职。
根据该提案，各州还可以指定其他活动来满足要求。此外，各州可以通过基于积分的系统调整每周求职门槛，以考虑当地劳动力市场状况，该系统允许申请失业援助的人为一项活动累积多个积分。
劳工部表示：“在这样的制度下，各州可以为合格的求职活动分配积分，并要求个人每个福利周至少积累五个积分。”
