Teacher's aide arrested in connection with NYC jogger's murder: Police
Later Sunday, the government filed court documents in the case, but they were sealed and inaccessible to the public.

The Iranian American Legal Defense Fund has called for a halt to the removal flights, saying in a news release that they would “reportedly mark the first deportation of Iranians to Iran since the U.S.-Iran war began.”

The group’s executive director, Yasmin Chubin, said in a statement Sunday that it was difficult to comprehend why the U.S. would forcibly deport Iranians, including asylum seekers, to Iran, amid ongoing military hostilities.
The consequences of removal, Chubin said, “could be irreversible and individuals may face persecution, torture, or death.”

At least one person who had been part of the scuttled flight volunteered to go back to Iran after nearly two years of detention, Rahnama said, out of desperation to leave what he described as inhumane imprisonment. It’s not clear how many other of the deportees may have volunteered to leave.
body_zh: 一架最终飞往伊朗的美国驱逐航班突然取消，该航班载有至少八名伊朗国民
洛杉矶——据一位与一些计划被遣返的被拘留者交谈的律师称，周日上午，美国一架经由巴基斯坦飞往伊朗的伊朗国民驱逐航班突然被取消。
代表一些伊朗被拘留者提出紧急动议的伊朗美国法律辩护基金会律师阿里·拉赫纳马表示，周日早上，至少八名伊朗人在亚利桑那州梅萨被装载上一架飞机，飞往格鲁吉亚，然后飞往巴基斯坦。他说，航班被取消，没有任何解释。
几天前该基金提起的民事诉讼中公开的法庭文件显示，特朗普政府就在十月中旬表示，计划通过一个未透露姓名的第三国将伊朗人驱逐到伊朗，即使那里的战争仍在继续。该诉讼于 7 月提起，指控美国政府非法与伊朗官员分享有关伊朗人在美国寻求庇护的机密信息。
2025年9月至2026年1月期间，共有3架驱逐航班飞往伊朗，驱逐了100多名伊朗国民。但政府在二月份开始的战争中确认了新计划，突显了其实施强硬移民镇压的决心，其中包括加大遣返力度，包括前往批评者认为可能危及回返者生命的地方。
美国国土安全部在周日回答美联社提问时表示，移民和海关执法局不会对“预期的遣返行动，包括航班时刻表、乘客名单、目的地或个案详细信息”发表评论，也不会确认未来的遣返行动。
声明称：“正如所承诺的那样，特朗普政府正在利用一切合法选择来实施历史上最大规模的驱逐行动。”
政府在 10 月份的法庭记录中没有具体说明何时进行驱逐。但据多名律师透露，在过去一周，大约有十几名被移民拘留的伊朗国民表示，他们被告知，他们将被安排乘飞机前往巴基斯坦，然后前往伊朗。后来，他们向国土安全部证实了这些计划。
据拉赫纳马称，周日登上航班的八名被拘留者受到了伊朗利益科（巴基斯坦驻华盛顿大使馆负责处理领事事务的伊朗代表处）的一名高级官员的探视，并被告知伊朗政府将把他们从巴基斯坦运送到伊朗。
在伊朗移民倡导组织提起的诉讼中，至少有十几名伊朗被拘留者表示，伊朗官员曾与他们联系，了解他们庇护申请的敏感信息。
总统乔·拜登的提名人、美国地区法官安娜·C·雷耶斯尚未对这些指控作出裁决，但命令美国政府就任何将伊朗人驱逐到伊朗或任何其他国家的最终计划提前 24 小时向法院发出通知，并在执行任何此类驱逐之前提前五天发出书面通知。
在周日提交的一份法庭文件中，国防基金列出了周日驱逐航班计划的情况，并辩称政府可能违反了法官关于提前通知驱逐计划的指示。
父亲因涉嫌让6岁女儿排队领取神奇宝贝卡而被捕
警方助理因涉嫌谋杀纽约市慢跑者而被捕
周日晚些时候，政府提交了该案的法庭文件，但这些文件被密封，公众无法查阅。
伊朗裔美国人法律辩护基金会呼吁停止驱逐航班，并在一份新闻稿中表示，这将“据报道标志着自美伊战争开始以来首次将伊朗人驱逐到伊朗”。
该组织执行董事亚斯明·丘宾 (Yasmin Chubin) 在周日的一份声明中表示，很难理解为什么美国会在持续的军事敌对行动中强行将包括寻求庇护者在内的伊朗人驱逐到伊朗。
丘宾说，驱逐的后果“可能是不可逆转的，个人可能面临迫害、酷刑或死亡。”
拉纳马说，至少有一名参与失事航班的人在被拘留近两年后自愿返回伊朗，因为绝望地想离开他所说的不人道的监禁。目前尚不清楚还有多少被驱逐者自愿离开。

title_en: Democrats plan to use new power to rein in Trump's education agenda. But their tools are limited
title_zh: 民主党计划利用新的权力来控制特朗普的教育议程。但他们的工具有限
summary: Democrats in Congress are gearing up to challenge President Donald Trump's education policies, including the dismantling of the U.S. Education Department.
summary_zh: 国会中的民主党人正准备挑战唐纳德·特朗普总统的教育政策，包括解散美国教育部
body_en: Collin Binkley, Associated Press Collin Binkley, Associated Press
Heather Hollingsworth, Associated Press Heather Hollingsworth, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democrats-plan-to-use-new-power-to-rein-in-trumps-education-agenda-but-their-tools-are-limited

WASHINGTON (AP) — Democrats in Congress are preparing to flex their soon-to-be majorities in opposition to some of President Donald Trump's marquee education policies, starting with the dismantling of the U.S. Education Department. But with Trump threatening to use his veto power, they may be limited to opening investigations and using federal funding as leverage.

The White House has given no sign of backing away from its campaigns to close the department and to end diversity, equity and inclusion policies. But Democrats are preparing to use their oversight and appropriations powers to push back against Trump administration decisions that have reverberated through schools and universities.

Rep. Bobby Scott of Virginia, the top Democrat on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, said he plans to "leave no rock unturned" as he takes the helm of the panel's investigative powers, which include authority to issue subpoenas and hold hearings.

The committee is preparing to explore the Trump administration's dismantling of the Education Department, its oversight of federal student loans and its anti-discrimination policies, Scott said. Under Trump, the Education Department has prioritized investigations into transgender issues while backing away from addressing systemic racism in schools.
A day after the midterm elections, Scott sent a letter to 10 federal agencies reminding them to preserve records that might become part of a congressional review.
Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat, called on Democrats to "hold the Trump administration accountable for dismantling the Department of Education and turning its back on students."

Trump officials denounced Democrats' plans, with Education Department spokesperson Savannah Newhouse saying they're plotting to "prematurely sabotage" Education Secretary Linda McMahon. White House spokesperson Liz Huston accused Democrats of failing American students with "disastrous leadership" before Trump returned to office.
Investigations aren't likely to stop Trump agenda

Congressional investigations can be used to apply political pressure and uncover how decisions were made, but they are unlikely to present a substantial brake on Trump's education policies that have outraged Democrats over the last two years. And with Trump pledging to veto Democratic bills he sees as harmful, there's little optimism for legislative countermeasures.

"We're very happy that this Congress is unlikely to pass legislation like the legislation that was passed last year," said Diana Autin, executive director of the SPAN Parent Advocacy Network, a nonprofit based in Newark, New Jersey.
Still, she said, "it's not very likely that they will be able to undo the harm that's already been done."

Democrats on the Senate Appropriations Committee are exploring harder checks through the budgeting process. Some are planning to add conditions to spending bills aimed at reining in the Trump administration's education agenda.

"I think there will be an interest in using the power of the purse to establish guard rails and prevent these abusive practices," Sen. Chris Van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat on the Appropriations Committee, told The Associated Press.

Last year, Democrats failed to secure broad language in a funding bill to block further dismantling of the Education Department. Now, with majorities in both chambers, they're preparing to try again. Van Hollen described it as one avenue to "stop the bleeding" but not necessarily to reverse the dismantling that has been done.

"It's a little harder to try to rebuild an entity just through an appropriations bill," he said. "But we can certainly try to prevent further damage and then seek to reverse the harm that's been done."

There's also interest in conditioning federal funding to rein in Trump's battle to reshape higher education, Van Hollen said, including the White House's repeated efforts to cut funding at Harvard and other prestigious universities. "That said," he added, "we're dealing with an administration that has demonstrated no respect for the law."
body_zh: 科林·宾克利，美联社 科林·宾克利，美联社
希瑟·霍林斯沃斯，美联社 希瑟·霍林斯沃斯，美联社
华盛顿（美联社）——国会中的民主党人正准备展示他们即将占据的多数席位，反对唐纳德·特朗普总统的一些重要教育政策，首先是解散美国教育部。但由于特朗普威胁要使用他的否决权，他们可能仅限于展开调查并使用联邦资金作为杠杆。
白宫没有表现出任何放弃关闭该部门以及终止多元化、公平和包容政策的行动的迹象。但民主党正准备利用其监督和拨款权力来反击特朗普政府的决定，这些决定在学校和大学中引起了反响。
众议院教育和劳动力委员会民主党领袖、弗吉尼亚州众议员鲍比·斯科特表示，他计划在掌管该委员会的调查权时“千方百计”，其中包括发出传票和举行听证会的权力。
斯科特说，该委员会正准备探讨特朗普政府对教育部的解散、对联邦学生贷款的监督以及反歧视政策。在特朗普的领导下，教育部优先调查跨性别问题，同时放弃解决学校中的系统性种族主义问题。
中期选举一天后，斯科特致信 10 个联邦机构，提醒他们保存可能成为国会审查一部分的记录。
马萨诸塞州民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 呼吁民主党人“追究特朗普政府解散教育部并拒绝学生的责任”。
特朗普官员谴责了民主党的计划，教育部发言人萨凡纳·纽豪斯表示，他们正在密谋“过早破坏”教育部长琳达·麦克马洪。白宫发言人利兹·休斯顿指责民主党在特朗普重返办公室之前以“灾难性的领导力”辜负了美国学生。
调查不太可能阻止特朗普的议程
国会调查可以用来施加政治压力并揭露决策是如何做出的，但它们不太可能对过去两年激怒民主党人的特朗普教育政策产生重大影响。由于特朗普承诺否决他认为有害的民主党法案，立法对策的前景不容乐观。
位于新泽西州纽瓦克的非营利组织 SPAN 家长倡导网络的执行董事戴安娜·奥廷 (Diana Autin) 表示：“我们很高兴本届国会不太可能通过像去年通过的立法那样的立法。”
不过，她说，“他们不太可能能够消除已经造成的伤害。”
参议院拨款委员会的民主党人正在探索通过预算过程进行更严格的检查。一些人计划在支出法案中增加条件，旨在控制特朗普政府的教育议程。
拨款委员会马里兰州民主党参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 告诉美联社：“我认为，利用钱包的力量建立护栏并防止这些滥用行为会有兴趣。”
去年，民主党未能在一项拨款法案中获得广泛的措辞来阻止进一步解散教育部。现在，在参众两院都拥有多数席位的情况下，他们正准备再次尝试。范霍伦将其描述为“止血”的一种途径，但不一定能扭转已经完成的拆除工作。
“仅仅通过拨款法案来重建一个实体有点困难，”他说。 “但我们当然可以尝试防止进一步的损害，然后寻求扭转已经造成的损害。”
范霍伦表示，人们也有兴趣调整联邦资金，以遏制特朗普重塑高等教育的斗争，包括白宫一再努力削减哈佛大学和其他著名大学的资金。 “话虽如此，”他补充道，“我们面对的是一个不尊重法律的政府。”

title_en: Hegseth faces impeachment resolution from a GOP member with little to lose
title_zh: 赫格斯面临共和党成员的弹劾决议，几乎没有什么损失
summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday over his handling of the Iran war and other alleged misconduct. Why it matters: The coming vote could mark the first impeachment of a Cabinet secretar
summary_zh: 众议员托马斯·马西（肯塔基州共和党）周一提出了针对国防部长皮特·赫格斯的弹劾条款，指控他处理伊朗战争等问题。
body_en: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday over his handling of the Iran war and other alleged misconduct.

Why it matters: The coming vote could mark the first impeachment of a Cabinet secretary during the second Trump administration and signal what's to come when Democrats take control of Congress next year.

What they're saying: Hegseth "will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law," Massie said Monday while reading the articles of impeachment on the House floor.

"Secretary Hegseth knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders to initiate war against a foreign nation… thereby substituting unlawful executive action for the constitutional and statutory judgment of Congress."
The other side: Hegseth dismissed the impeachment push as politically motivated "noise" Monday, telling reporters that he and his team aren't worried with the push.
The Department of Defense didn't immediately respond to Axios' request for comment.

Catch up quick: Massie first introduced the articles of impeachment prior to the House going into recess so members could campaign. He reintroduced the resolution Monday, restarting a two-legislative-day clock for House leaders to act.
Massie and other members of Congress accuse Hegseth of defying Congress by continuing the unpopular war in Iran despite legislative efforts to shut it down.

Three of the eight articles accuse Hegseth of violating congressional war powers in Iran. The others allege misconduct involving civilian casualties, strikes on suspected drug boats, retaliation against Sen. Mark Kelly, the capture of Nicolás Maduro and military operations in Yemen.
Hegseth has reportedly been among the most ardent supporters of the war, telling Trump that the conflict would be easy to win.
Eight months later, that doesn't appear to be true.

Between the lines: Republicans who previously resisted reining in the administration's war effort might be more willing to impeach Hegseth now that voters have delivered a strong rebuke of the administration and its war during the 2026 midterms.
And with dozens of House and Senate members retiring or leaving Congress, it's possible the YOLO caucus might decide Hegseth should be the fall guy.
House GOP leaders are bracing for defections, Axios reported Sunday .
What we're watching: Even if the House impeaches Hegseth, removing him from office would require a two-thirds vote in the Republican-controlled Senate.

body_zh: 众议员托马斯·马西（肯塔基州共和党）周一提出了针对国防部长皮特·赫格斯的弹劾条款，指控他处理伊朗战争和其他涉嫌不当行为。
重要性：即将到来的投票可能标志着特朗普第二届政府期间对内阁部长的首次弹劾，并预示着民主党明年控制国会时将会发生什么。
他们在说什么：马西周一在众议院宣读弹劾条款时表示，如果允许赫格塞斯继续留任，他的行为方式与他的职责和法治严重不符，他将仍然对宪法构成威胁。
“赫格塞斯国务卿故意执行和实施对外国发动战争的非法命令……从而用非法行政行动取代了国会的宪法和法定判决。”
另一面：周一，赫格斯将弹劾推动视为出于政治动机的“噪音”，并告诉记者，他和他的团队并不担心弹劾推动。
国防部没有立即回应 Axios 的置评请求。
快速赶上：马西在众议院休会之前首先介绍了弹劾条款，以便议员们可以进行竞选活动。他周一重新提出了该决议，重新启动了两天的立法时间，供众议院领导人采取行动。
马西和其他国会议员指责赫格塞斯藐视国会，尽管立法部门努力制止伊朗战争，但仍继续进行不受欢迎的战争。
八篇文章中的三篇指责赫格塞斯侵犯了国会对伊朗的战争权力。其他人指控不当行为涉及平民伤亡、袭击涉嫌贩毒的船只、对参议员马克·凯利的报复、尼古拉斯·马杜罗的被捕以及在也门的军事行动。
据报道，赫格斯是这场战争最热心的支持者之一，他告诉特朗普，这场冲突很容易获胜。
八个月后，情况似乎并非如此。
言外之意是：既然选民在 2026 年中期选举期间对政府及其战争进行了强烈谴责，之前拒绝控制政府战争努力的共和党人可能更愿意弹劾赫格塞斯。
随着数十名众议院和参议院议员退休或离开国会，YOLO 核心小组可能会决定赫格斯应该成为替罪羊。
据 Axios 周日报道，众议院共和党领导人正准备叛逃。
我们正在关注的内容：即使众议院弹劾赫格塞斯，将他免职也需要共和党控制的参议院三分之二的票数支持。

title_en: California's fifth consecutive Catholic governor exemplifies the faith's deep roots
title_zh: 加州连续第五任天主教州长体现了信仰的深厚根基
summary: Xavier Becerra's recent election as California governor highlights the state's unique blend of Catholicism and progressive politics.
summary_zh: 泽维尔·贝塞拉 (Xavier Becerra) 最近当选为加州州长，凸显了该州天主教与进步政治的独特融合。
body_en: Krysta Fauria, Associated Press Krysta Fauria, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/californias-fifth-consecutive-catholic-governor-exemplifies-the-faiths-deep-roots

LOS ANGELES (AP) — As he campaigned for California governor, Xavier Becerra reflected on the way his Catholic upbringing informs his politics. "The sanctity of life is something that's really ingrained in you," the Democrat and former U.S. health and human services secretary said earlier this year.

He then explained his rationale, confounding to some, for supporting abortion rights. Becerra exemplifies how Catholicism's deep roots often go hand in hand with California's progressive reputation. That complexity is a snapshot of a larger reality — that American Catholics are in many ways a politically mixed bag.

"There is no Catholic vote," said David Gibson, the director of Fordham University's Center on Religion and Culture. White evangelicals for Republicans or Black Protestants for Democrats are more politically reliable religious groups, he said.

With Becerra's win this week , California has elected five consecutive Catholic governors — a remarkable streak indicative of Catholicism's enduring influence. "Catholicism is part of the fabric of California culture the way Puritan Protestantism is part of the New England regions," Gibson said.
Catholic voters — especially Latinos — helped elect Becerra, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of roughly 100,000 midterm voters. He became the state's first elected Latino governor.

Beginning with Gray Davis, who took office in 1999, four of those five governors also have been Democrats. Some have been more vocal about their faith than others — notably Jerry Brown, who was a seminarian in the 1950s.

California is home to more Catholics than any other U.S. state. A Pew Research Center poll in 2024 found that 25% of adults in California identify as Catholic, accounting for almost half of the state's Christians.
But numbers aside, Catholicism has been woven into the fabric of the state for centuries.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom (right) and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom (left) visit the Divine Providence Chapel where Monsignor Oscar Arnulfo Romero was assassinated by a gunman in 1980, during a part of their three-day visit in San Salvador in 2019. Photo by Salvador Melendez/AP

From economically progressive strains of Catholic social teaching and explicit rejections of the death penalty to official teachings against abortion and in vitro fertilization, Catholic theology rarely fits neatly into political categories, which helps explain the unpredictable voting habits.

Take Gov. Gavin Newsom, whose strong support of abortion rights is at odds with Catholic leadership. Yet his announcement this week that he planned to change more than 500 death sentences in the state to life in prison without the possibility of parole was celebrated by the California Catholic Conference, the public policy organization representing the church in California.

"I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us," Newsom said in a public letter.

Some leaders within the church have subverted Trump administration policies, like San Bernardino Bishop Alberto Rojas, who last year formally excused parishioners from their weekly obligation to attend Mass following immigration detentions on parish properties in the diocese.

Others have taken high-profile conservative stances, like San Francisco Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone, who in 2022 barred U.S. Rep. Nancy Pelosi, a Catholic, from receiving Communion over her support of abortion rights.

About 2 in 10 voters in the California governor's race were Catholic, and they mostly voted for Becerra, according to The AP Voter Poll. About 6 in 10 Catholic voters supported Becerra, while about 4 in 10 voted for his Republican opponent Steve Hilton.
About 7 in 10 Latino Catholics voted for Becerra, while white Catholics were split between Becerra and Hilton.
Those complex political patterns are also reflected nationally. Catholics were split evenly between Democrats and Republicans.

洛杉矶（美联社）——在竞选加州州长时，泽维尔·贝塞拉反思了自己的天主教成长经历对他的政治影响的方式。这位民主党人、前美国卫生与公共服务部部长今年早些时候表示：“生命的神圣性是你根深蒂固的。”
然后他解释了他支持堕胎权的理由，这让一些人感到困惑。贝塞拉体现了天主教的深厚根基往往与加州进步的声誉紧密相连。这种复杂性是一个更大现实的缩影——美国天主教徒在很多方面都是政治上的混杂体。
“没有天主教徒的投票，”福特汉姆大学宗教与文化中心主任大卫·吉布森说。他说，共和党的白人福音派或民主党的黑人新教徒是政治上更可靠的宗教团体。
随着贝塞拉本周的胜利，加州连续选举出五位天主教州长——这一显着的连胜表明了天主教的持久影响力。 “天主教是加州文化的一部分，就像清教徒新教是新英格兰地区的一部分一样，”吉布森说。
根据美联社选民民意调查（对大约 10 万中期选民进行的调查），天主教选民，尤其是拉丁裔选民，帮助贝塞拉当选。他成为该州第一位当选的拉丁裔州长。
从1999年上任的格雷·戴维斯开始，这五位州长中有四位是民主党人。有些人比其他人更直言不讳地表达自己的信仰，尤其是 20 世纪 50 年代的神学院学生杰里·布朗 (Jerry Brown)。
加利福尼亚州的天主教徒人数比美国任何其他州都多。皮尤研究中心 2024 年的一项民意调查发现，加州 25% 的成年人是天主教徒，几乎占该州基督徒的一半。
但撇开数字不谈，几个世纪以来天主教已经融入到国家的结构中。
加利福尼亚州州长加文·纽瑟姆（右）和他的妻子詹妮弗·西贝尔·纽瑟姆（左）在 2019 年圣萨尔瓦多为期三天的访问期间参观了神圣普罗维登斯教堂，奥斯卡·阿努尔福·罗梅罗主教于 1980 年在这里被枪手暗杀。照片由 Salvador Melendez/美联社拍摄
从天主教社会教义的经济进步和对死刑的明确拒绝，到反对堕胎和体外受精的官方教义，天主教神学很少完全符合政治范畴，这有助于解释不可预测的投票习惯。
以州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 为例，他对堕胎权的强烈支持与天主教领导层不一致。然而，他本周宣布计划将该州 500 多名死刑判决改为终身监禁且不得假释，这一消息受到代表加州教会的公共政策组织加州天主教会议的庆祝。
纽瑟姆在一封公开信中表示：“我采取这一行动是因为我坚信，国家批准的杀戮与加州的价值观不相容，破坏了我们法律体系的基础，并削弱了我们每个人的能力。”
教会内的一些领导人颠覆了特朗普政府的政策，比如圣贝纳迪诺主教阿尔贝托·罗哈斯(Alberto Rojas)，他去年在教区教区财产上移民被拘留后，正式免除教区居民每周参加弥撒的义务。
其他人则采取了高调的保守立场，例如旧金山大主教萨尔瓦多·科迪莱昂 (Salvatore Cordileone)，由于天主教徒美国众议员南希·佩洛西 (Nancy Pelosi) 支持堕胎权，他于 2022 年禁止她接受圣餐。
据美联社选民民意调查显示，在加州州长竞选中，大约十分之二的选民是天主教徒，他们大多投票给贝塞拉。大约十分之六的天主教选民支持贝塞拉，而大约十分之四的人投票给他的共和党对手史蒂夫·希尔顿。
大约十分之七的拉丁裔天主教徒投票支持贝塞拉，而白人天主教徒则分为贝塞拉和希尔顿。
这些复杂的政治模式也反映在全国范围内。天主教徒在民主党和共和党之间各占一半。
